Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
6.x: Both are true and R explains A: Ambedkar explained that 'Union' was used because the federation is not the result of an agreement among the States and no State can secede – 'an indestructible Union of destructible States'.

6.s: A Bill to form a new State under Article 3 can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the:
6.x: The Bill needs the President's recommendation and is referred to the State legislature for its views.

6.s: Which of the following statements about the Article 3 procedure is correct?
o: Parliament must accept the views of the State legislature.
Such a Bill needs a special majority of Parliament.
Parliament is not bound by the views of the State legislature.
Such a Bill must also be referred to a Union Territory legislature.
6.x: The views of the State legislature are not binding; a simple majority suffices and no reference is needed for a Union Territory.

6.s: Which union territory became the 25th state of India?
6.x: Goa, a UT since 1962, became the 25th State on 30 May 1987 (56th Amendment). Sikkim was the 22nd, Mizoram the 23rd and Arunachal the 24th.

6.s: Sikkim State is
o: a part of the Indian territory
the 21st State of the Indian Union
6.x: Sikkim was an associate State only in 1974-75; by the 36th Amendment (1975) it became the 22nd full State, so today it is simply part of the Indian territory. It was not the 21st State.

6.s: The State that was first admitted into the Indian Union as an associate State
6.x: Sikkim became an 'associate State' by the 35th Amendment (1974) – the first and only one – before becoming a full State by the 36th (1975).

6.s: The Indian State that was given just the status of associate in 1974 and got the status of a full state in 1975 by the Amendments of the Constitution is
6.x: Sikkim was made an associate State by the 35th Amendment (1974) and a full State by the 36th Amendment (1975).

6.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the formation as full States of the Indian Union?
6.x: Nagaland (1963), Haryana (1966), Sikkim (1975), Arunachal Pradesh (1987).

6.s: Mizoram has been granted the status of a State by which of the following Constitutional Amendment?
6.x: Mizoram became a State on 20 February 1987 under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 and the 53rd Amendment. The 55th was Arunachal Pradesh.

6.s: Sikkim became a state of India under-
6.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (36th Amendment); it is added as option 5.
Sikkim became a full State by the 36th Amendment (1975), which is not offered. The 35th Amendment (printed key) only made it an 'associate State', so no option is correct.

The state of Bombay was split into Gujarat and Maharashtra

6.x: Telangana, the 29th State (2 June 2014), has Hyderabad as its capital. Panaji is Goa's capital and Silvassa a UT capital.

6.x: Punjab in its present form dates from 1966 (Haryana carved out), later than Andhra Pradesh (1956), Gujarat (1960) and Karnataka (formed as Mysore in 1956, only renamed in 1973).

2. Himachal Pradesh
3. Haryana
4. Sikkim
6.x: Andhra Pradesh (1953/1956), Haryana (1966), Himachal Pradesh (1971), Sikkim (1975) → 1, 3, 2, 4.

6.x: The 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim a full State, the 22nd. The 35th (1974) only made it an associate State.

6.s: In which year did the State Jharkhand come into existence?
6.x: Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000).

6.s: By which of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution was Mizoram granted Statehood?
6.x: Mizoram became a State by the 53rd Amendment Act, 1986 (in force 20 February 1987); the 52nd was the anti-defection law.

6.s: In which year were Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya granted Statehood?
6.x: Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became full States on 21 January 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971 (the Act is of 1971, statehood came in 1972).

6.s: The name of the Laccadive, Minicoy and Aminidivi islands was changed to Lakshadweep by an Act of Parliament in
6.x: The Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands were renamed Lakshadweep in 1973 by an Act of Parliament (the same year Mysore became Karnataka).

6.s: The first state newly created after the inauguration of Indian constitution
6.x: Andhra State (1 Oct 1953, carved out of Madras) was the first new State created after the Constitution came into force, and the first linguistic State. Kerala came in 1956, Gujarat in 1960 and Tripura in 1972.

6.s: The year during which the Indian Constitution was amended thrice for the creation of new States is
6.x: Three new States – Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand – were created in 2000. Strictly, they were made by Reorganisation Acts under Arts. 3-4, not by constitutional amendments. (Moved to row 6.)

6.s: How many States and Union Territories are present in India?
6.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
6.x:
29 States and 7 UTs was the count before the J&K Reorganisation Act (2019) and the DNH–Daman & Diu merger (2020) — now 28 States and 8 UTs (Indian_Polity Part 1 p.48)
India now has 28 States and 8 UTs (since 26 January 2020). The printed answer, 29 States and 7 UTs, was correct only between 2014 and August 2019 (now 28 and 8).

6.s: How many Union Territories (excluding island territories) are located on the coast of India?
6.x: Leaving out the island UTs (A&N, Lakshadweep), only Puducherry and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu lie on the coast, so two. Delhi, Chandigarh, J&K and Ladakh are inland.

6.s: India is at present a union of
6.x:
Updated to the latest (Nov 2026): India has 28 States and 8 UTs since 26 Jan 2020 (DNH and Daman & Diu merger), unchanged Nov 2026. (When this paper was set, the answer was: 28 States + 7 Union Territories.) Source: https://knowindia.india.gov.in/states-uts/
28 States + 7 UTs was the count of 2012 — now 28 States and 8 UTs (Telangana 2014, J&K → 2 UTs 2019, DNH–Daman & Diu merger 2020) (Indian_Polity Part 1 p.48)
In 2012 India had 28 States and 7 UTs, so A was correct then (now 28 States and 8 UTs, since 26 January 2020).

6.s: At present how many States and Union Territories are there in India?
6.x: India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories (since 26 January 2020).

6.s: Which Union Territories are included in the term "State" in article 54 of the Constitution relating to election of President?
o: Only the National Capital Territory of Delhi
Only the Union Territory of Puducherry
The National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry
6.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
6.x: The Explanation to Article 54 (70th Amendment, 1992) says 'State' includes the NCT of Delhi and the UT of Puducherry, so their elected MLAs vote in the President's election. Other UTs are not included.

6.s: The following region does not come under the territorial jurisdiction of Bombay High Court

B. Pondicherry
C. Delhi
6.x: Delhi is the only UT with a High Court of its own. Chandigarh is under the Punjab and Haryana HC and Puducherry under the Madras HC, so C only.

b. The Governor of Kerala is concurrently the Administrator of Lakshadweep.

6.s: By which Constitutional amendment Delhi was given the status of National Capital Region?
6.x: The 69th Amendment (1991) gave Delhi special status as the National Capital Territory with a legislature (Art. 239AA).

o: Diu is an island in the Gulf of Khambhat
Daman and Diu were separated from Goa by the 56th
Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under French colonial
6.x: Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under Portuguese, not French, rule until 1954, so D is incorrect. Goa became a State in 1987, Diu is an island in the Gulf of Khambhat, and Daman and Diu were separated from Goa in 1987.

6.s: Which one of the following Union Territories of India is the smallest in terms of geographical area?
6.x: Lakshadweep (about 32 sq km) is the smallest UT by area, far smaller than Chandigarh, Daman and Diu or DNH.

6.x: Goa is a State (since 1987); A&N, Daman and Diu and Puducherry are UTs.

6.x: Lakshadweep is the smallest UT (about 32 sq km); Ladakh is the largest.

6.s: The Union Territories are administered by the:
o: President through administrators appointed by him
6.x: Article 239: every Union Territory is administered by the President through an administrator appointed by him.

6.s: In which Union Territory, is the administrator designated as Lieutenant Governor?

6.x: Andaman and Nicobar Islands has a Lieutenant Governor (as do Delhi, Puducherry, J&K and Ladakh); Chandigarh, Dadra-Nagar Haveli-Daman-Diu and Lakshadweep have Administrators.

6.x: 28 States in 2003 (after Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand in 2000); 29 from 2014 to 2019; 28 again since 31 October 2019 (and 8 UTs).

o: Ladakh became a separate Union Territory in 2019.
Jammu and Kashmir was the first State to be converted into Union Territories.
6.x: Before August 2019 India had 29 States; the count fell to 28 when Jammu and Kashmir, the first State so downgraded, became two Union Territories.

6.x: Lakshadweep is the smallest UT by area.

6.x: Yanam is in Andhra Pradesh, Mahe in Kerala, and Puducherry and Karaikal in Tamil Nadu.

6.x: It was under Portuguese rule.

6.x: The merged UT came into being on 26 January 2020.

6.x: Under Article 239(2), the Governor of Punjab administers Chandigarh.

6.s: The States' Reorganisation Act, 1956 divided the Indian territory into ............ zones

6.x: The S.K. Dhar Commission (1948) recommended reorganisation on administrative convenience, not language. The Fazl Ali Commission broadly accepted language as a basis.

6.s: On which date in 1953 the States Reorganization Commission was set up by Government of India
6.x: Nehru announced the States Reorganisation Commission on 22 December 1953, after Andhra State was formed. The MHA resolution formally constituting it is dated 29 December 1953, which is not among the options.

6.s:
Consider the following statement and answer using codes given below:
1. The term ‘Union of States, has been used in the constitution because Indian States, have no right of separation.
2. S.K. Dhar Commission had given preference to administrative convenience rather language for re-organisation of States.
3. Congress Committee including Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya was not in favour of reorganisation of States on the basis of language.
Which of the following statement is/are correct?
6.x: All three are correct: Ambedkar said the States have no right to secede (hence 'Union'); the Dhar Commission preferred administrative convenience; the JVP Committee rejected language as the basis.

6.s: The Commission for Reorganisation of States on the basis of language was established in-
6.x: The States Reorganisation Commission was set up in December 1953, which is not offered; the reorganisation on a linguistic basis it recommended was carried out in 1956 (SRA, 1 Nov 1956), so 1956 is the intended answer.

6.s: Who among the following was not the member of Reorganization Commission which was formed in 1953 and whose recommendations were taken into account for the States Reorganization Act, 1956?
6.x: The SRC members were Fazl Ali (chairman), K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was in the JVP Committee, not the SRC.

6.s: In which year were the Indian States reorganized on the recommendation of the State Reorganisation Commission?
6.x: The SRC reported in 1955 and the States Reorganisation Act came into force on 1 November 1956, so the States were reorganised in 1956.

6.s:
Consider the following statements with respect to 'Creation of States':
a. On October 1, 1953, the Andhra State was created. The State comprised the Telugu-speaking districts of Madras State.
b. In 1956, as a part of the States Reorganization Act, the States in India were arranged on linguistic basis. This resulted in the creation of new States. Andhra Pradesh was created by merging Andhra State with the Telugu speaking area of the Hyderabad State.
c. Bombay State was split into the linguistic States of Gujarat and Maharashtra on 1 May 1960 by the Bombay Reorganisation Act.

6.x: All three are correct: Andhra State (1 Oct 1953) took the Telugu districts of Madras; in 1956 it merged with the Telugu areas of Hyderabad to form Andhra Pradesh; and the Bombay Reorganisation Act split Bombay into Gujarat and Maharashtra on 1 May 1960.

6.s: Which Amendment is related to the State Reorganisation Act, 1956?
6.x: The 7th Amendment, 1956 gave effect to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956: it ended the Part A/B/C/D classification and created States and Union Territories. The 17th, 12th and 19th Amendments deal with other matters.

6.s: What was the capital city of the Andhra state that was separated from the Madras state in 1953?
6.x: Kurnool was the capital of Andhra State when it was formed in 1953. Hyderabad became the capital only in 1956.

6.s: Andhra Pradesh was created as a language based state in–
6.x: The first language-based State, Andhra State, was formed on 1 October 1953; the State named Andhra Pradesh came in 1956 by merging Telangana. The question means the 1953 linguistic State (exam key 1953).

6.s: After Independence, in which year were the Indian States reorganized on the linguistic basis?
6.x: Andhra State (1953) was the first linguistic State, but large-scale reorganisation on a linguistic basis came with the States Reorganisation Act in 1956.

6.s: In which year the States Reorganisation Commission was appointed?
6.x: The States Reorganisation Commission (Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar, H.N. Kunzru) was appointed in December 1953 and reported in 1955.

6.s: Prior to 1953, India was territorially divided into how many types of States?
6.src: APPSC Hyderabad Metro Water Works Managers 2012
6.x: In 1950 the Constitution had a four-fold classification – Part A, Part B and Part C States and Part D territory – abolished by the SRC/7th Amendment in 1956 (printed key: 3).

8.x: Under Art. 358, a National Emergency (war/external aggression) automatically suspends Art. 19, the Right to Freedom; other FRs need a Presidential order under Art. 359, and Arts. 20-21 are never suspended.

8.s: X was addressing a seminar on the meaning of the term 'law' as provided under Article 13, Part III of the Constitution of India. X explained that the meaning of the term 'law' in the Constitution of India was very comprehensive. It included ordinances, orders and even rules and regulations. Y pointed out that the term 'law' in Article 13 also included custom or usage having in the territory of India the force of law, to which 'X' was not convinced. Based on the above, select the correct conclusion from the options given below:
o: X is correct in the interpretation of law, including the view on non-inclusion of custom.
The view of Y that 'law' included custom is not correct.
The views of both 'X' and 'Y' are correct.
The view of only Y is correct.

Any reason considered desirable by the executive
An ordinance that is immune from judicial review

FRs are **qualified, not absolute**: restrictions must be **by law**, on grounds the Constitution names, and **courts judge reasonableness**.
xa: **Art. 19** lists **11** restriction grounds in all.
⚠ "FRs are absolute" is **wrong** (PYQ **2019**).
Under **Art. 13(3)**, "law" includes an **ordinance** — so no ordinance escapes judicial review.

n: The Directive Principles of State Policy are non-justiciable. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]

27.x: All three: the VP is elected for five years, is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and on a vacancy acts as President only until a new President is elected (max six months).

27.s: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the office of Vice-President?
o: The Vice-President office is modelled on the lines of the American Vice-President.
The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament.
All doubts and disputes in connection with the election of the Vice-President are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court of India.

If the office of the Vice-President falls vacant due to resignation, removal, death, or any other reason, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha acts as Vice-President until a new Vice-President is elected.
27.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
27.x: Not correct: (d). The Constitution is silent on who acts as Vice-President in a vacancy; the Deputy Chairman only performs the Chairman's duties in the Rajya Sabha. (a)-(c) are true – the office is modelled on the American VP, elected by both Houses, disputes go to the SC.

27.s: Identify the wrong statement with regard to Vice President of India.
o: Vice President cannot act as Chairperson of Rajya Sabha while he is officiating as President of India.

The election disputes of Vice President of India are decided by the Supreme Court
27.x: Wrong: (b). The VP is removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by a majority of all its then members (effective majority) and agreed to by the Lok Sabha – not two-thirds. He does not chair the RS while acting as President, has a casting vote, and the SC decides his election disputes.

27.s: In case of the office of President of India falls vacant, the new President is to be elected within ____ months of the vacancy.

27.x: Under Article 67(a) the Vice-President resigns by writing addressed to the President – not the PM or Parliament.

27.x: On the President's death the VP acts as President only until a new President is elected, which must be within six months (Art. 62) – not for the remaining term.

27.s:
If Vice-President of India has to discharge the duties of President of India in his absence due to some reasons, then what is/are true for such duration?
(i) In this duration, Vice-President holds the post of Chairman of Council of States
(ii) In this duration, Vice-President will get the emolument of President
(iii) If in this duration, Vice-President resigns, then Chief Justice of India will perform the duties of President of India
27.x:
Most books and keys: (ii) and (iii). Strictly, the Art. 64 proviso only bars him from performing the Chairman's duties while acting – he is not removed from the post of Chairman.
(ii) and (iii): while discharging the President's functions the VP draws the President's emoluments and does not perform the Chairman's duties (the Deputy Chairman presides); if he resigns, both offices are vacant and the CJI discharges the President's functions under the 1969 Act.

27.s: A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President of India can be proposed in –
27.x: Under Art 67(b) the removal resolution is moved only in the Rajya Sabha, then needs the Lok Sabha's agreement; it is not moved in the Lok Sabha or a joint sitting.

27.s: Which of the following is true regarding the Prime Minister of India?
o: The President appoints the Prime Minister
The Lok Sabha elects the Prime Minister
The Prime Minister works as leader of the parliamentary party in the Lok Sabha

o: Constitutionally, the Prime Minister should definitely be a member of the Lok Sabha.

xs: A **Vote of Credit** is an **unexpected, blank-check grant** for an **emergency** or **indefinite** demand — option **(3)**.

An **advance grant** for part of the year is a **Vote on Account**; **₹100** is a **token cut**.

**Exceptional grant:** not part of the current service of any year.
⚠ **115** = supplementary, additional, excess; **116** = vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional.

Assertion (A): An MP or MLA may be treated as having voluntarily given up party membership even without formally resigning.
Reason (R): Conduct such as publicly campaigning for an opposition party can constitute voluntarily giving up membership.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
36.x: Both are true: a member can be held to have given up party membership without resigning, because conduct such as campaigning for a rival party counts. R explains A.
36.tq: Recall that conduct can amount to giving up membership.
n: Voluntarily giving up party membership is broader than formal resignation and includes conduct. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 210-212]
An MP or MLA can be considered to have voluntarily given up party membership by publicly campaigning for an opposition party. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 210-212]
An MP or MLA can be considered to have voluntarily given up party membership without submitting a formal resignation letter. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 210-212]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
"**Voluntarily giving up membership**" is **broader** than **formal resignation** — it can be inferred from **conduct**.
**Publicly campaigning** for an **opposition party**, even without a resignation letter, counts — which explains A.
xa: **Ravi S. Naik v UoI (1994)**: voluntarily giving up membership is **not the same as resigning**.
**G. Viswanathan (1996)**: an **expelled** member **still belongs** to his party; joining another party = giving up membership.
Other ground: **voting or abstaining contrary to the party whip** without **prior permission** (**Para 2(1)(b)**).

36.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding a Presiding Officer under the Anti-Defection Law?
o: A Presiding Officer cannot rejoin the original party after demitting office.
A Presiding Officer may face disqualification for joining another political party after vacating office.
A Presiding Officer may face disqualification for joining another political party while holding office.
A Presiding Officer can voluntarily give up party membership upon election to the Chair.
36.x: Option A is incorrect: a presiding officer may give up party membership on election to the Chair and rejoin the party after leaving office. Joining another party, during or after the term, disqualifies them.
36.tq: Discriminate rejoining the original party from joining another.
n: A presiding officer is disqualified for joining another political party while holding office. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 210-212]
A presiding officer is disqualified for joining another political party after vacating office. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 210-212]
A presiding officer may voluntarily give up party membership upon election to the Chair. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 210-212]
A presiding officer may rejoin the original party after demitting office. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 210-212]
xs: The incorrect statement is that a **Presiding Officer cannot rejoin the original party after demitting office** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
A Presiding Officer **may voluntarily give up** party membership on **election to the Chair** and **rejoin** the original party after demitting office.
He is disqualified only for **joining another political party** while holding office or after vacating it — so options (2), (3), (4) are true.
xa: This exception is **Para 5**, covering **Speaker/Deputy Speaker/Chairman/Deputy Chairman**; it is **in force**.
Criticism: Indian Speakers **do not resign from their party**, so they are seen as partisan.
The Presiding Officer decides defection petitions under **Para 6**.

36.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Subhash Desai judgment (May 2023)?

36.s: What does 'resort politics' refer to in the context of anti-defection and floor tests?
o: Sending legislators abroad for parliamentary training
Dissolving the legislature before a confidence motion
Sequestering legislators before a floor test to prevent poaching
Suspending legislators who abstain from voting

xs: Resort politics = **sequestering legislators before a floor test** to stop **poaching** — option **(3)**.
It is one of the **ways around the law**, along with the **resignation route** and **merger misuse**.
xa: **Resignation route**: MLAs **resign** to cut the majority mark (Karnataka **2019**, MP **2020**).

36.s: What do legislators do in the 'resignation route' used to avoid disqualification proceedings?
o: Seek prior permission from the Election Commission before switching parties
Resign, lowering the majority mark, and later re-contest on the new party's ticket

Merge into the new party without resigning

36.s: What does the proposal to limit the whip and disqualification under the anti-defection law to confidence and money votes seek to ensure for legislators?
o: Vote against every money bill without party discipline
Avoid all party whips during the entire legislative term
Dissent even on a confidence motion without consequences
Dissent freely on matters that do not threaten the government's survival

xs: Legislators could **dissent freely on votes that do not threaten the government's survival** — option **(4)**.
The whip would apply only to **confidence and no-confidence motions and money bills**.

xa: Backers: **Dinesh Goswami (1990)** and **Law Commission (1999)**.

36.s: Which of the following statement is correct regarding Parliamentary Privileges ?
36.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test 2024 (Notification No. 12/2023), held 17-03-2024, Paper-I General Studies (GS/1G/100) · Q54
36.x: Freedom from arrest (during a session and 40 days before and after) covers only civil cases, not criminal or preventive detention cases. Privileges are both collective and individual, outsiders can be punished for contempt, and contempt is the wider idea.
o: Parliamentary Privileges are the privileges that are enjoyed collectively by each House of the Parliament, and not by the Members individually.
Only Members can be punished for contempt by reprimand and admonition but not outsiders.
The phrase 'Breach of Privilege' has wider implications than the 'Contempt of the House'.
The Members cannot be arrested during the session of Parliament but this privilege is available only in civil cases and not in criminal cases or preventive detention cases.

Both the President and Governor have discretionary powers
Both the President and Governor have no discretionary powers
39.x: The Constitution expressly mentions discretion only for the Governor (Art. 163(1)); the President has no constitutional discretion, only situational discretion.

39.s: The orders passed by the Governor of a State (Article 163) fall in four categories. Find out the category which is NOT subject to Judicial Review.
o: Where the Governor acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
Where the Governor acts without the aid and advice of the Council of his own discretion
Where the Governor enters and acts in legislative matters
Where the Governor addresses the legislature
39.x: Decisions taken in the Governor's own discretion are made final by Art. 163(2), so they are not subject to judicial review; acts on aid and advice are reviewable.

39.s: The President may appoint a Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union Territory. Such Governor in the administration of the Union Territory shall exercise his functions
o: With the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers of the State
As such administrator independently of his Council of Ministers
Under the direct supervision of the President
With the help of a council appointed by the Union Territory
39.x: Under Art. 239(2), a Governor appointed administrator of an adjoining UT acts as such independently of his State Council of Ministers.

39.s:
Which of the following are the discretionary powers given to the Governor of a State?
1. Sending a report to the President of India for imposing the President's rule
2. Appointing the Ministers
3. Reserving certain bills passed by the State Legislature for consideration of the President of India
4. Making the rules to conduct the business of the State Government
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Constitutional discretion covers the report recommending President's Rule (Art. 356) and reserving Bills for the President (Art. 200). Ministers are appointed on the CM's advice, and rules of business are made on advice – not discretion.

39.s:
The governor of the state, may act independently from the consultation of Legislative Assembly when -
(1) The Government has to prove its majority in the session of Legislative Assembly.
(2) To terminate the Chief Minister.
(3) To reserve any bill for the consideration of President of India.
(4) To send back a bill to Legislative Assembly for reconsideration.
(5) To seek the consultation with High Court.
Choose the correct answer from the following code:
39.x: Asking the Government to prove majority, dismissing a CM who lost confidence, reserving a Bill and returning a Bill are acts the Governor takes himself; consulting the High Court is no power of the Governor, so code (1,2,3,4).

39.s:
Which of the following are the discretionary powers given to the Governor of a State?
1. Sending a report to the President of India for imposing the President’s Rule
2. Appointing the Ministers
3. Reserving certain bills passed by the State Legislature for consideration of the President of India
4. Making rules to conduct the business of the State Government
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
39.x: Statements 1 (report under Art. 356) and 3 (reserving Bills, Art. 200) are constitutional discretion; appointing Ministers (CM's advice) and making rules of business (Art. 166(3)) are not.

39.s:
Which of the following are the discretionary powers given to the Governor of the state?
I. Sending a report to the President of India for imposing the President’s rule.
II. Appointing the ministers.
III. Reserving certain Bills passed by the State Legislature for the consideration of the President of India.
IV. Making the rules conduct the business of the State Government.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
39.x: I (Art. 356 report) and III (reservation under Art. 200) are constitutional discretion; appointing Ministers and making rules of business are done on advice.

39.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. The Constitution of India explicitly mentions that in certain spheres the Governor of a State acts in his/ her own discretion.
II. The President of India can, of his/her own, reserve a bill passed by a State Legislature for his/ her consideration without it being forwarded by the Governor of the State concerned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: I is correct: Art. 163(1) expressly mentions matters the Governor decides in his discretion. II is wrong: the President cannot on his own reserve a State Bill – only the Governor reserves it under Art. 200.

39.s: If a Chief Minister loses majority in the Legislative Assembly, he:
o: Continues in office until the next general election
Can be removed only by impeachment
Must resign or may be dismissed
39.x: A Chief Minister who loses majority must resign or may be dismissed; once a new Chief Minister is sworn in, the former ceases to hold office.
xa: Dismissing a ministry that has lost majority is **situational discretion**.
**West Bengal:** **Mamata Banerjee** refused to resign after losing (**5 May 2026**); the **Art. 164 "pleasure"** clause lets the Governor dismiss her.
**S.R. Bommai (1994):** majority to be tested **on the floor**.

39.s: In May 2026, after Mamata Banerjee refused to resign despite losing the election, which provision was cited as allowing the Governor to dismiss a Chief Minister who has lost majority?
o: The bar on court inquiry in Article 163(3)
39.x: Ministers hold office during the Governor's pleasure under Article 164, which allows dismissal of a CM who has lost majority. Article 356 is President's Rule, Article 163(3) bars inquiry into ministerial advice, and Article 361 grants the Governor immunity.
39.tq: CM who lost majority → Art. 164 pleasure.
xs: The **Art. 164 "pleasure" clause** lets the Governor dismiss a CM who has lost majority — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mamata Banerjee** refused to resign after losing (**5 May 2026**).
**Art. 356** is President's Rule, **Art. 163(3)** bars inquiry into advice, **Art. 361** gives immunity.
xa: Dismissing a ministry that has lost majority is **situational discretion**.
**Art. 164(1):** ministers hold office during the **Governor's pleasure**.
Once a new CM is sworn in, the old one **ceases**.

39.s:
Assertion (A): The Governor can reserve a Bill for the President even when the Council of Ministers advises otherwise.
Reason (R): The Governor is not bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers in all matters.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
39.x: Both are true: the Governor can reserve a bill for the President against ministerial advice because the Governor is not bound by that advice in every matter. R explains A.
39.tq: Ask whether limited discretion explains acting against advice.
n: The Governor can reserve a Bill for the President even when the Council of Ministers advises otherwise. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 29-32]
The Governor is not bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers in all matters. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 29-32]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Governor may **reserve a Bill** for the President **even against the Council's advice** — a **discretionary power**.
This is possible because he is **not bound** by the Council of Ministers' advice in **all** matters.
xa: Reserving a bill (**Art. 200**), recommending President's Rule (**Art. 356**) and seeking information (**Art. 167**) = **constitutional discretion**.
Appointing a CM in a **hung Assembly** = **situational discretion**.
The only **mandatory** reservation: a bill that **derogates from the powers of the High Court**.
Governor's discretion is **wider than the President's**.

39.s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Governor of Nagaland have special responsibility for law and order?
39.x: Article 371A gives the Governor of Nagaland special responsibility for law and order; 371H does the same for Arunachal Pradesh.

39.s: Which of the following statements about Article 163 is correct?
o: The Council of Ministers advises the Governor in all matters without exception
The Governor's discretion is narrower than the President's
Courts may inquire into ministerial advice to the Governor
The Governor's decision on whether a matter is within his discretion is final
39.x: Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision final, and the Governor has wider discretion than the President.

Match List-I with List-II:

39.x: A TAC has up to 20 members, about three-fourths of them ST MLAs.

39.x: The order is a pre-poll alliance, then the single largest party, then a post-poll coalition.

39.s:
Identify the correct statement/statements with regard to Jammu and Kashmir
A. Governor's Rule is possible in Jammu And Kashmir
B. President's Rule can be imposed in Jammu and kashmir under the article 356 of the Indian Constitution
C. Financial Emergency cannot be imposed in Jammu and kashmir under the article 360 of the Indian Constitution
D. Right to Property is still a fundamental right in Jammu & Kashmir.
39.x:
Updated to the latest (Nov 2026): J&K has been a Union Territory since 31 Oct 2019 (Art. 370 inoperative; upheld by SC Dec 2023): no Governor's Rule, President's Rule under Sec. 73 of the 2019 Act, Art. 360 applies, property not a FR — none of A-D holds. (When this paper was set, the answer was: A, B, C, D.) Source: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15240
Art. 370 was made inoperative and J&K became a UT on 31 Oct 2019 (J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019) — now none of A-D holds; President's Rule there is under Sec. 73 of that Act (indiacode.nic.in)
In 2019, before the August 2019 changes, all four were true for J&K: Governor's Rule under Sec. 92 of the J&K Constitution, Art. 356 thereafter, Art. 360 not applicable, and the right to property still a FR there.

39.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
39.x: Telangana (formed 2014) and Chhattisgarh (2000) have never been under President's Rule (true as of Nov 2026).

39.s: Mark the incorrect option with respect to the President's rule in an Indian state.
o: The President's rule is imposed under powers conferred by Article 356 of the Constitution
Article 355 imposes a duty upon the Centre to ensure that all state governments in India function under the provisions given in the Constitution
The state will be administered by the Governor on behalf of the President.
The central cabinet passes the state bills and budget when the legislative assembly is suspended or dissolved under the President's rule.
39.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer Paper-III (Indian Con
39.x: Incorrect: under President's Rule Parliament (Art. 357), not the Union Cabinet, passes the State's Bills and budget. Art. 356 is the power, Art. 355 the Centre's duty, and the Governor administers the State for the President.

39.x: President's Rule is imposed under Art. 356; Manipur's latest spell began on 13 Feb 2025 (revoked Feb 2026). Art. 352 is National Emergency.

39.x: Stem garbled: Governor's Rule (Sec. 92 of the J&K Constitution) existed only in the former J&K, so Manipur, Mizoram and Meghalaya ALL lacked it – no single option fits 'no provision'. The printed 'Mizoram' has no basis (and the old explanation was from another question).

39.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Punjab); it is added as option 5.
Official key: PEPSU (1953) — the earliest of the printed options. Strictly the first was Punjab, 1951 (Laxmikanth; Rocket notes 'sources vary').
The first President's Rule was in Punjab on 20 June 1951; PEPSU (1953) was the second, and UP, Travancore-Cochin and Bihar came later.

39.s: After the Ayodhya incident in 1992, Vidhan Sabha in some States was dissolved. Out of the following, in which state the Vidhan Sabha was not dissolved?
39.x: After Ayodhya (Dec 1992) the BJP Assemblies of UP, MP, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan were dissolved under Art. 356; Bihar's was not (Bihar's brief President's Rule came in 1995).

39.x: President's Rule is mainly imposed on the Governor's report under Art. 356, though the President may also act 'otherwise'.

39.s: The President may issue a proclamation of emergency under Article 356 on receipt of a report from the ……… of a state.
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
39.x: Art. 356 is invoked on a report from the Governor of the State (or otherwise) – not the Chief Justice, Advocate-General or Speaker.

39.s: If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 356 of the Constitution in respect of a particular state, then
o: The Assembly of the state is automatically dissolved
The powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by or under the authority
Article 19 is suspended in that state
The President can make laws relating to that State
39.x: Under Art. 356(1)(b) the powers of the State Legislature become exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament. The Assembly is suspended or dissolved, not automatically dissolved; Art. 19 is not suspended; Parliament, not the President, makes the laws.

39.s: If the State fail to carry out directives of the Union Government, the President canto
o: Send reserve police to the State
Impose president rule on the State
Direct the Governor to dismiss the State council of ministers
39.x: If a State fails to comply with Union directions, Art. 365 lets the President hold that its government cannot be carried on per the Constitution and impose President's Rule (Art. 356).

39.s: In S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994), the dismissal of the Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh governments was upheld on which ground?
o: Loss of majority on the floor
39.x: The nine-judge bench in S.R. Bommai held secularism to be a basic feature and upheld those dismissals on that ground.

39.s: What did the Supreme Court hold in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) about a proclamation under Article 356?
o: reviewable only after approval of the proclamation by the State Legislature
subject to judicial review, and the Union must disclose relevant material
beyond judicial review in all circumstances under Article 74(2)
reviewable only by the Governor of the State concerned on reference
39.x: The nine-judge Bench in S.R. Bommai held that an Article 356 proclamation is subject to judicial review and that the Centre must show relevant material supporting it.
39.tq: Test the constitutional safeguard against an extreme claim of complete immunity from judicial review.
xs: **S.R. Bommai (1994)**: an **Art. 356** proclamation is **subject to judicial review** and the Centre **must show relevant material** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not beyond review, and review is by **courts**, not the Governor.
xa: Majority tested by a **floor test**, not in **Raj Bhavan**.
Assembly **not dissolved before Parliament approves**; ministry can be **restored**.
**Secularism** is a basic feature; a government violating it can be dismissed.

39.s: After the Ayodhya events of December 1992, the BJP governments of Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and which other State were dismissed?
39.x: The BJP governments of UP, MP, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh were removed; Bommai upheld the dismissals of MP, Rajasthan and HP.
xa: **Bommai:** **secularism** is a basic feature; a government violating it can be dismissed.
Bommai also held proclamations **judicially reviewable**.
Majority to be tested by a **floor test**, not in Raj Bhavan.

39.s: On which date did the latest spell of President's Rule in Manipur begin?
39.x: The latest spell began on 13 February 2025 (Manipur's 11th) and was revoked on 4 February 2026.
xa: Manipur was the **APPSC 2024** key for **Art 356**.
President's Rule overall: used **over 125 times**.

39.s: Under the former Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir, for how long at most could Governor's Rule continue?
o: 1 year under Article 360 of the Constitution of India
6 months under Section 92 of the J&K Constitution
3 months under Article 356 of the Constitution of India
2 years under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019
39.x: In the former Jammu and Kashmir constitutional arrangement, Governor’s Rule was imposed under Section 92 of the J&K Constitution for six months, after which Article 356 could apply.
39.tq: Discriminate between the special provision, its duration and the later Article 356 stage.
xs: In former J&K, **Governor's Rule** ran **6 months** under **Sec 92 of the J&K Constitution**, then **Art 356** — option **(2)** is correct.
Example: **2018**.
xa: After **2019**, President's Rule ran under the **Reorganisation Act** until **Oct 2024**.
Under Art 356 generally: **6 months** at a time, maximum **3 years**.
**Art. 360** is the **Financial Emergency**, not J&K Governor's Rule.

39.s: Under which Article of the Constitution can President's Rule be imposed when a State fails to comply with the directions of the Union?
39.x: Article 365 treats failure to follow Union directions as a situation in which the State's government cannot be carried on per the Constitution, so Article 356 may be used.

39.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. President's Rule may be imposed on the report of the Governor or otherwise.
2. Failure of a State to comply with Union directions is a ground for President's Rule under Article 365.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Both statements are correct: under Article 356 President's Rule may be imposed on the Governor's report or otherwise, and Article 365 makes non-compliance with Union directions a ground.

39.x: It can last at most three years, in six-month extensions; beyond one year only with a National Emergency and an EC certificate.

o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

o: President may declare his assent to the bill

39.x: Art. 200 gives the Governor four options, including reserving a Bill for the President; Art. 201 covers the President's options afterwards.

39.x: The Governor reserves a Bill for the President under Art. 200; Art. 201 is the President's action on it and Art. 356 is President's Rule.

39.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct? Under Article 200 of the Constitution of India, the Governor of a State may
I. withhold his assent to a bill passed by the State Legislature.
II. reserve the bill passed by the State Legislature for reconsideration of the President.
III. return the bill, other than a money bill for reconsideration of the Legislature.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below

39.s: The reservation of State Bills for the consideration of the President is an example of which of the following?
39.x: Reservation of Bills by the Governor for the President is a classic example of central control over the States.

o: Permanent representative of the Union Cabinet in the State
Final constitutional sovereign of the State
Judicial guardian of the State Legislature
Guide, philosopher and friend of the government

39.s: In State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu, decided on 8 April 2025, which timeline was associated with the Governor's action on Bills?

n: Sikkim has the smallest State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Sikkim Legislative Assembly has 32 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]

41.s: What is the quorum for a sitting of a Legislative Assembly of 70 members?
41.x: Quorum is 10 members or one-tenth of the total membership, whichever is greater. For a 70-member House, 10 is greater than 7.
41.tq: Apply the ‘whichever is greater’ rule rather than simply calculating one-tenth.
xs: Quorum is **10 members**, which is greater than one-tenth of **70** (= **7**) — option **(2)**.
Rule (**Art. 189(3)**): **10 members or one-tenth** of the House, **whichever is greater**.
So option (1), **7**, is only the one-tenth figure; **35** and **70** are not the rule.
xa: The **Speaker** adjourns or suspends the House for **lack of quorum**.
**Art. 189** also: the Speaker has a **casting vote** on a tie.
Normal Assembly strength: **60-500** (**Art. 170**).

41.s: Which of the following statements most accurately explains the primary difference between the powers of the State Legislative Assembly and the State Legislative Council in the process of lawmaking for ordinary bills?
o: Both houses must agree for an ordinary bill to become law

41.x: For ordinary Bills the Assembly has the final say: the Council can only delay (3 months, then 1 month) and the Assembly's will prevails; there is no joint sitting.

41.s: Regarding the disagreement between the two Houses of the State Legislature, which of the following is correct?
o: The Council can permanently block a bill
The only power of the Council is to interpose some delay in the passage of the bill
A joint session is convened to resolve the dispute
The Governor has the final say
41.x: The Council cannot permanently block a Bill; its only power is to interpose delay (3 months, then 1 month). There is no joint sitting and the Governor has no final say.

41.s: If a bill is introduced in the Legislative Council of the State and sent to the Legislative Assembly for approval but if the Legislative Assembly rejects the bill, what is the next course of action?
o: Joint sitting of both the Houses
Council may send the bill back to the Assembly for reconsideration
Bill may be sent to the Governor for examination
The fate of the bill ends
41.x: A Bill that originates in the Council and is rejected by the Assembly ends – there is no joint sitting in States and no re-passage mechanism for Council Bills.

o: Joint sitting of both the Houses

Bill may be sent to the Governor for examination
The fate of the bill ends
41.x: A Bill that originates in the Council and is rejected by the Assembly ends – there is no joint sitting in States and no re-passage mechanism for Council Bills.

n: Article 227 gives High Courts power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 189-193]
A High Court exercises administrative superintendence over subordinate courts and tribunals throughout its territorial jurisdiction. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 189-193]
A High Court exercises judicial superintendence over subordinate courts and tribunals throughout its territorial jurisdiction. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 189-193]

The Armed Forces exception to High Court superintendence is provided by Article 227(4). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 189-193]
xs: The incorrect statement is that superintendence **extends to courts and tribunals under laws relating to the Armed Forces** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Article 227(4)** excludes **military tribunals**.
Art. 227 gives **administrative and judicial superintendence** over all subordinate **courts and tribunals** in its territory — so (1), (3), (4) are correct.
xa: It is **revisional** and can be exercised **suo motu**.
⚠ The SC has **no** Art. 227-type power.
Similarly, SC's **Art. 136(2)** SLP does not lie against **Armed Forces Courts**.

the 80th Amendment (2000) moved railway-fare taxes from Art. 269 into the Art. 270 divisible pool — now Art. 269 assigns to the States only taxes on inter-State sale/purchase and consignment of goods (Laxmikanth Ch15).

the 101st Amendment (2016) removed excise on medicinal and toilet preparations from Art. 268 — now such preparations are taxed under GST (CGST + SGST) (Laxmikanth Ch15 p.231).

64.s: VVPAT slips must be counted in which of the following circumstances?

xs: **VVPAT slips must be counted wherever EVM data do not match Form 17C** — so option **(1)** is correct.

D. Introduction of Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan
82.x: The Madras Corporation came first (1688), then Ripon's Resolution (1882), the 1919 Act and Rajasthan's Panchayati Raj (1959). The order is A, B, C, D.
n: Lord Ripon’s 1882 Resolution recognized Lord Ripon as the Father of Local Self-Government in India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The Government of India Act, 1919 made Local Self-Government a Transferred Subject under provincial dyarchy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Rajasthan was the first Panchayati Raj State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The first Panchayati Raj system in Rajasthan was established in Nagaur District. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The first Panchayati Raj system was established in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Madras established the first Municipal Corporation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The first Municipal Corporation was established in Madras in 1688. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: Correct order: **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Madras** Municipal Corporation (**1688**) → **Lord Ripon's Resolution** (**1882**) → **GoI Act, 1919** (Transferred Subject) → **Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan** (**2 October 1959**).
xa: **Bombay** and **Calcutta** corporations followed Madras in **1726**.
**Lord Mayo's** resolution on financial decentralisation came in **1870**.
UP set up corporations in the five **KAVAL towns** (**1953**); UP Municipal Corporations Act **1959**.
**Andhra Pradesh** was the **second** Panchayati Raj state.

107.s: Which of the following was the custom practised during the ancient period that allows married women to cohabit with a designated male for the sole purpose of procreating a child if her husband was impotent or had died?
107.x: Niyoga is the ancient custom in which a wife cohabits with a designated man to bear a child when her husband is impotent or dead; the other options are not names of this custom.

108.x: The Nayar tarawad is a matrilineal (and matrilocal) joint family.

108.s: Which of the following group/s is/are identified as pro-matriarchal group/s?
o: Nagas in Nagaland and Iyengars in Tamil Nadu
Nairs in Kerala and Khasis in Meghalaya
Meenas in Rajasthan and Mundas in Jharkhand
Santals in Jharkhand and Baidyas in West Bengal
108.src: TSPSC Tutors in Medical Education, Dental Assistant Surgeon,
108.x: The Nairs of Kerala and the Khasis of Meghalaya are the classic matrilineal ('pro-matriarchal') groups; the others are patrilineal.

108.s: The statement that "the children born to a married husband and his wife must have no legal genitor" applies to which caste or community in ancient times?
108.x: Among the Nairs the husband had no legal paternity – children belonged to the mother's tharavad and had no legal father (Gough's classic case).

108.s: Matrilineal family system belongs to them.
108.x: The Nairs follow the matrilineal tharavad system; Namboodiris, Muslims (mainland) and Coorgs are patrilineal.

108.s: Who among the following will be present along with woman in 'Tharavad'?
o: Her sons, daughters, daughters' daughters, sons
Her husband, her sons, sons' daughters, sons
108.x: A Nair tharavad consists of a woman, her brothers and sisters and her own and her sisters' sons and daughters (and daughters' children); husbands and sons' wives belong to their own tharavads.

108.s: Which of the following Muslim communities is matrilineal?
108.x: Of the printed options the Navayats of the Konkan–Kanara coast follow matrilineal descent (D'Souza 1955); Memons and Bohras are patrilineal. Option 1 is garbled ('Figure of Sri Lanka', probably the Moors of Sri Lanka, also matrilineal), so the key is uncertain.

108.s: Which of the following communities is NOT matrilineal?
108.x: The Khasis, Garos and Nairs are matrilineal; the Namboodiri Brahmins and the Nagas are patrilineal.

108.s: In matrilineal societies, the authority held by the maternal uncle is known as:
108.x: Avunculate is the special authority of the mother's brother; levirate and sororate are marriage customs.

108.s: In which year was India's National Family Planning Programme, the first such national programme in the world, launched?
108.x: India launched the world's first National Family Planning Programme in 1952, which also made it the first in Asia.

108.s: Which Articles of the Directive Principles first gave constitutional recognition to family welfare?
108.x: Family welfare was first recognised in the DPSP through Articles 39 and 42.

108.s:
Which of the following tribes practice couvade?
A. Khasi
B. Toda
C. Spoon
D. Ho
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
108.x: Couvade (kuhana prasuti – the husband imitating his wife's pregnancy and birth taboos) is reported among the Khasi and the Toda, i.e. A and B; 'Spoon' is a garbled item and the Ho are not the textbook example (printed key: B, C, D).

109.s: Veeramushtis are a dependent caste of ........ caste.
109.src: TSPSC Technical Assistant in Ground Water Department 2016
109.x: The Viramushtis are a dependent bard/begging caste attached to the Komatis (Vaishyas) of Telugu country, who traditionally maintain them.

109.s: ____ enunciated seven cultural traits of caste.
109.x: J.H. Hutton (Caste in India, 1946) listed the cultural traits of caste (endogamy, commensal and food restrictions, hereditary occupation, pollution etc.); printed key kept. Ghurye gave six features; Dumont stressed hierarchy and purity-pollution.

109.s: Who states that the Varna Model has produced a wrong and distorted image of caste?
109.x: M.N. Srinivas, in 'Varna and Caste' (1962), wrote that 'the varna model has produced a wrong and distorted image of caste', since the real unit is the local jati, not the four varnas.

109.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of caste?
109.x: Caste features are endogamy ('inter-marriage' = antar-vivaha, marriage within), hereditary occupation and commensal (meal) rules; complexion is not a feature of caste. Off-topic (society), moved.

109.s: Caste possesses which two dimensions in relation to social organisation?
109.x: Caste has a vertical dimension expressed through ranking and a horizontal dimension expressed through grouping into separate communities.
109.tq: Recall the paired dimensions and distinguish ranking from grouping.
xs: Caste has a **vertical** dimension (**ranking**) and a **horizontal** dimension (**grouping**) — option **(2)**.
Ranking reflects **hierarchy**; grouping reflects separate, **endogamous** communities.
xa: **Ghurye**'s **segmental division** and **hierarchy** match these two dimensions.
**Dumont**: hierarchy rests on **pure vs impure**.
**Dipankar Gupta**: castes = **discrete communities**; "difference" ≠ "hierarchy".

109.s: Which of the following is NOT a cultural trait associated with caste?
109.x: Universal inter-caste commensality is contrary to the commensal taboos associated with caste. Pollution by touch, untouchability and Sanskritic rituals are recognised traits.
109.tq: Identify the option that reverses a central prohibition.
xs: **Universal inter-caste commensality** is **not** a caste trait — option **(1)** — it contradicts **commensal taboos**.
**Commensal taboos**, **untouchability** and **pollution-by-touch** are all listed traits.
xa: The fourth trait is **Sanskritic rituals**.
Ghurye's list includes restrictions on **feeding and social intercourse**.
**Marriott**: castes ranked by exchange of food, water and services.

109.s: The word 'caste' is derived from the word 'casta' of which language?
Enumeration of caste in the Indian Census began in:
109.x: Caste was enumerated from the 1871 Census; 1931 recorded 4,147 castes.

109.s:
Assertion (A): G.S. Ghurye listed the lack of free choice of occupation among the features of caste.
Reason (R): Ghurye's 'Caste and Race in India' was published in 1932.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
109.x: Both are true: lack of free choice of occupation is one of Ghurye's six features, set out in 'Caste and Race in India' (1932). But the year of the book does not explain the feature, so R is not the explanation of A.

109.s: Which Sikh group constitutes the largest Scheduled Caste component among the groups mentioned?
109.x: Mazhabi Sikhs are identified as the largest Scheduled Caste component among the Sikh groups mentioned.
109.tq: Distinguish the Scheduled Caste component from the other named Sikh communities.
xs: **Mazhabi Sikhs** are the **largest SC component** among Sikhs — option **(1)**.
**Khatri**, **Arora** and **Jat** are listed Sikh castes but not the SC component.
xa: The fourth listed Sikh caste: **Ramgarhia**.
Sikhs were added to the **SC Order** in **1956**.
⚠ **1956** = Sikhs; **1990** = Buddhists.

109.s: Who among the following saw caste as a colonial construct shaped by the Census?
109.x: Nicholas Dirks and Susan Bayly argued that caste in its modern form was shaped by colonial rule and the Census.

a. F.G. Bailey

109.s: Which of the following is not correct regarding the Caste System in Ancient India ?
o: There was a proliferation of castes due to growth in guilds.
The caste system became more complex with the influx of foreigners.
The caste system became more complex when tribal regions were brought under cultivation.
The caste system led to perfect social stability in ancient India.

109.x: Guild growth, foreign influx and the absorption of tribal regions multiplied castes and made the system more complex; caste never produced 'perfect social stability', so D is the wrong statement.

110.s: The first synchronous and comprehensive census was conducted in India in the year?
110.src: Assistant Social/BC/Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-I 20
110.x: The first synchronous (all-India, simultaneous) Census was held in 1881; the 1872 Census under Lord Mayo was non-synchronous.

110.s: The first modern synchronous and comprehensive census in India was conducted in:
110.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
110.x: The first Census (1872, under Lord Mayo) was non-synchronous, while the first synchronous Census was held in 1881, so 1881 is correct. 1871 is the tempting option but it was not synchronous.

110.s: Which one of the following represents a dispute associated with the proposed caste enumeration?
o: The Opposition opposed digital enumeration but supported abolition of the questionnaire
The Supreme Court rejected the caste count, while the Centre demanded its cancellation
The Centre treated OBC lists as classes rather than castes, while the Opposition sought withdrawal of the questionnaire
The Centre abolished all SC and ST enumeration, while the Opposition sought separate electorates
110.x: The Centre dropped OBC lists on the ground that they represented classes rather than castes; the Opposition sought that the questionnaire be scrapped. The Supreme Court upheld the caste count.
110.tq: Compare the positions of the Centre, Opposition and Supreme Court without reversing their roles.
xs: The **Centre** dropped OBC lists as "**classes, not castes**", and the **Opposition** wanted the **questionnaire scrapped** — option **(3)**.
The **SC upheld** the caste count, so (2) is wrong.
xa: Pre-test: **6-20 Jul 2026**, with an **open column**.
Debate: **open column vs pre-coded** caste list; fragmentation vs data for the **50% cap**.
Population Enumeration due **Feb 2027**.

110.s: India's first, non-synchronous Census (1872) was held under the Viceroy:
110.x: It was held under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous Census came in 1881 under Ripon.

110.s: Which of the following statements about caste enumeration is correct?
o: The 1951 Census was the last full caste count
The 1872 Census was held under Lord Ripon
Since 1951 OBCs are enumerated by caste in the Census
The SECC 2011 was run outside the Census Act, 1948
110.x: The SECC was run by the Rural Development Ministry; 1872 was under Mayo, only SCs and STs are enumerated since 1951, and 1931 was the last full count.

110.s: Census 2027 will be India's first digital Census and the first caste count since:
110.x: Census 2027 will be the first full caste count since 1931.

To counter Brahmin supremacy in politics
To support the Home Rule Movement
To promote commercial and industrial activities

110.x: The Justice Party (South Indian Liberal Federation, 1916–17) was formed to counter Brahmin dominance in politics and public services and to secure representation for non-Brahmins.

111.s: Which of the following States has the lowest concentration of tribal population?
111.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa

111.s: Which State has the largest tribal population as per 2011 census
111.x: Census 2011: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population (about 1.53 crore, ~21% of India's STs); Sikkim, Himachal and Nagaland are far smaller in number.

111.x: Gahira Guru (Rameshwar Kanwar) was a social reformer of the Kanwar tribe of Chhattisgarh (Sanatan Sant Samaj). He was not a Gond, Kamar or Oraon.

111.x: The Jarawa are a Negrito tribe of the Andaman Islands. Munda belong to Jharkhand, Kota to the Nilgiris and Kadar to Kerala/Tamil Nadu.

111.x: The Onge of Little Andaman, a PVTG, show a sustained decline in population. Meena, Gond and Munda populations are growing.

111.s: Which of the following states is not a habitat of the Kuki tribe in India?
111.x: The Kukis live mainly in Manipur, Assam, Nagaland and Mizoram; Arunachal Pradesh is not a Kuki habitat (its tribes are Adi, Nyishi, Apatani, Monpa, Mishmi).

o: None of the above/More than one of the above

Match the following:
List-I (Tribe)
A. Gaddi
B. Bhutia
C. Santhal
D. Khasi
List-II (State)
1. Sikkim
2. Meghalaya
3. Himachal Pradesh

Select the correct answer using the code given below:

111.s: According to Census 2011, which is the largest tribe of India?
111.x: The Bhil is the largest tribe and the Gond the second-largest; Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population by number.

111.s: According to Census 2011, which State has the largest Scheduled Tribe population by number?
111.x: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population; Mizoram has the highest ST share among States.

Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Tribe)
a. Santhal
b. Jarawa
c. Shompen
d. Toda
List-II (Habitat)
i. Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu)
ii. Great Nicobar
iii. Jharkhand (largest tribe there)
iv. Andaman Islands
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
111.x: Santhal – largest tribe of Jharkhand; Jarawa – Andaman Islands (Negrito); Shompen – Great Nicobar; Toda – Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu).

111.s: To add any tribe as a Scheduled Tribe (ST) in India, which process must be followed as per the Constitution?
o: Article 242 - President by notification declares a tribe as Scheduled Tribe.
Article 342 - Governor of the concerned state issues a notification.
Article 342 - President by notification declares a tribe as Scheduled Tribe.
Article 242 - Governor of the concerned state issues a notification.
111.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
111.x: Under Article 342(1) the President, by public notification after consulting the Governor, specifies the Scheduled Tribes of a State/UT. Article 242 has nothing to do with STs, and the Governor does not notify.

111.s: In which year was TRICOR (Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Tribes Cooperative Finance Corporation) established?
111.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-I
111.x: TRICOR, the AP Scheduled Tribes Co-operative Finance Corporation, is keyed as set up in 1976 (the year the Krishna district ST co-operative corporation was also registered). Web sources found give no clear founding date; the older Andhra ST finance body of 1955-56 became GCC in 1970.

111.s: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India gives the authority to the Indian Parliament to include any community or group or exclude any community or group from the list of Scheduled Tribes?
111.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
111.x: Article 342(2) lets only Parliament, by law, include or exclude a community from the ST list. Article 341 is the SC equivalent, 340 the Backward Classes Commission, 339 Union control over ST welfare.

111.s: Under the Constitution of India, certain tribes have been specified as
111.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Planning & Regulation Secretary
111.x: The Constitution (Art. 342, 366(25)) speaks of 'Scheduled Tribes'; it does not use 'hill tribes' or 'backward tribes'. The printed key was missing.

111.s: How many communities are notified as Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh?
111.x: Andhra Pradesh has 34 notified STs; 12 is the PVTG count of the joint AP-Telangana list.

111.s: Scheduled Tribes are defined in which Article of the Constitution?
111.x: Article 366(25) defines STs as communities deemed under Article 342; 366(24) defines SCs.

111.s: The first order specifying Scheduled Tribes under Article 342(1), the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, was issued by the:
111.x: The President notifies the first list; ST lists are State/UT-specific.

111.s: Which of the following statements about Scheduled Tribes is correct?
o: The Lokur Committee (1965) laid down five tests for identifying STs.
The criteria for identifying STs are laid down in the Constitution.
The Lokur Committee was set up in 1975.
111.x: The criteria come from the Lokur Committee of 1965, not the Constitution; STs form 8.6% of the population.

111.s: According to Census 2011, Scheduled Tribes form what percentage of India's population?
111.x: STs form 8.6% of India's population; SCs form 16.6%.

111.s: In which tribe touching the plow (plough) and filling the house are prohibited for women?
111.x: Among the Santhals, women are forbidden to touch the plough and to thatch (cover) the roof of a house. 'Qadiah' is not a tribe name; the printed key (option 1) looks like a garbled entry.

111.s: Which set of objects is interchanged within "Kula"?
111.x: In the Kula ring of the Trobriand Islands (Malinowski), shell necklaces (soulava) and armshells or bracelets (mwali) circulate in opposite directions.

111.s: The division of labour in aboriginal society is mainly based on this.
111.x: Division of labour in aboriginal (tribal) society rests mainly on age and sex (gender), not on caste.

111.s: In tribal societies "age-groups" were considered as one of the basis of which of the following?
111.x: Age-groups (age-sets) were a basis of stratification in tribal societies, ranking members by seniority.

111.s: From which language does the word 'tribe' come?
111.x: The word 'tribe' comes from the Latin word 'tribus'.

111.s: Shifting (slash-and-burn) cultivation in North-East India is called:
111.x: It is Jhum in the North-East; Podu is the term in Andhra Pradesh and Bewar in Madhya Pradesh.

111.s: Totemism among tribes, a clan's sacred bond with an animal or plant, goes with:
111.x: Members of a totemic clan may not marry within it: totemism goes with clan exogamy.

111.s:
Assertion (A): B.S. Guha classified the Jarawa and Onge as Negrito.
Reason (R): H.H. Risley classified Indian tribes racially into Dravidian and Mongoloid types.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
111.x: Both are true, but they are two separate racial classifications: Guha's (Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid) and Risley's (Dravidian, Mongoloid). Risley's scheme does not explain Guha's placing of the Jarawa and Onge.

III. There are 95 PVTGs officially notified in the country so far.

111.x: The PVTG concept is associated with the Dhebar Commission (1960-61); India has 75 PVTGs.
xa: The **PTG** category followed (dated **1973**); renamed **PVTGs in 2006**.
The 75 are spread over **18 states + 1 UT (A&N)**.
⚠ CDX wrongly dates the Commission itself to **1973**.

111.s: Which of the following are the smallest Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) by population?
111.x: The Sentinelese and the Andamanese are the smallest PVTGs; the Sahariyas are the largest.

111.x: Andhra Pradesh had 4,92,552 PVTG people under PM-JANMAN, among the top three States.

111.s: The Shompen controversy over the Great Nicobar project concerns protection under:
o: The A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956 and habitat rights under Section 3(1)(e) of the FRA
The Sixth Schedule provisions for autonomous district councils and the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956

The National Service Scheme was started in 1959.
PM-Vidyalaxmi is a mid-day meal scheme for schools.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the Assam Movement:
I. The Assam Movement led by All Assam Students' Union (AASU) was started in the year 1983.
II. The objective of the Assam Movement is to identify the migrant people, protect and provide constitutional, legislative and administrative safeguards to the Bangladeshi Migrants in Assam.
III. The Assam Movement was officially ended on 15th August, 1989 after coming to an understanding with the Government of India which found official expression in the Memorandum of Understanding popularly known as the Assam Accord.
Which of the above given statements is/are correct?
121.x: The AASU-led Assam Movement ran 1979-85 (not from 1983), targeted illegal migrants (did not protect them) and ended with the Assam Accord of 15 Aug 1985 (not 1989) – all three are wrong.

121.s: What followed the NEET paper leak protests, which began at Jantar Mantar and turned nationwide?
o: A Supreme Court ban on protests at Jantar Mantar
121.x: The protests began at Jantar Mantar, turned nationwide and were followed by a ministerial resignation (5 Aug 2026).

121.s:
Match List-I (Student movement) with List-II (State / centre):
List-I
a. Nav Nirman (1974)
b. JP movement (1974)
c. AASU movement (1979-85)
d. Telangana student movements (1969; 2009-14)
List-II
i. Assam
ii. Bihar
iii. Gujarat
iv. Osmania University

121.x: Nav Nirman – Gujarat; JP movement – Bihar (both 1974, a common trap); AASU – Assam; Telangana student movements – Osmania University.

121.x: Derozio of Hindu College inspired the Young Bengal movement.

121.x: The movement ended with the Assam Accord of 15 August 1985.

121.x: Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku 1966; Srikakulam peasant (girijan) movement 1967; Jai Andhra 1972; anti-arrack Sara Nishedha Udyamam 1991-92 (Dubagunta).

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Jai Andhra agitation (1972-73) was ended by the Six-Point Formula of 1973.
Reason (R): The Jai Andhra agitation followed the Supreme Court's decision upholding the Mulki Rules.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
121.x: Both are true: the agitation began after the SC upheld the Mulki Rules and was ended by the Six-Point Formula (1973). But R gives the cause of the agitation, not why it ended, so R does not explain A.

121.s: The anti-arrack movement (Sara Nishedha Udyamam) of 1991-92 in Andhra Pradesh was started by the rural women of:
121.x: It began with the women of Dubagunta village in Nellore district.

121.s: The 'Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku' agitation of 1966 is associated with the fast of:
121.x: T. Amrutha Rao's fast led the agitation for the Visakhapatnam steel plant.

121.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of youth unrest?
o: Identity crisis among youth is a cause of youth unrest.
The generation gap is growing as families become nuclear.
Families in India are increasingly becoming nuclear.
The generation gap is shrinking as families become nuclear.
121.x: The identity crisis and generation gap grow, not shrink, as Indian families become nuclear.

121.s: About how many people join India's working-age group each year (2021-31)?
121.x: About 9.7 million join the working-age group each year, which feeds jobless-growth unrest.

121.s: As per Census 2011, youth (15-24 years) formed about what share of India's population?
121.x: Youth aged 15-24 numbered about 231 million (19.1%); adolescents (10-19) numbered about 253 million.

121.s: Which of the following statements about youth unemployment is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh's youth unemployment was below the national rate
In Andhra Pradesh, rural youth unemployment was higher than urban
In Andhra Pradesh, urban youth unemployment was higher than rural youth unemployment
121.x: In AP (PLFS 2023-24) urban youth unemployment was 22.7% against 15.5% rural; AP's 17.5% was above the national rate.

121.s: According to the ILO (2026), the global youth unemployment rate is about:
121.x: In AP (PLFS 2023-24) youth unemployment was 17.5%, above the national rate.

121.s: As per Census 2011, the female literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh is:
121.src: APPSC Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges (Notification No. 26/2018) - General Studies & Mental Ability (Paper-I), computer-based test, held 15-09-2020 · Q119
121.x: Census 2011 put the female literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh at about 59%.

121.s: In India, the proportion of population in the working age group (15 - 64 years) is
121.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test - General Studies & Mental Ability, held 20-04-2008 · Q80
121.x: The key gives about 56% of India's population in the 15-64 working-age group.

121.s: As per the 4th National Family Health Survey, how many females are there in the State of Andhra Pradesh per 1000 males ?
121.src: APPSC Group-I Services Screening Test (Notification No. 36/2016) - General Studies & Mental Ability (single paper, Booklet Series A), held 07-05-2017 · Q100
121.x: NFHS-4 (2015-16) reported a sex ratio of 1,020 females per 1,000 males for Andhra Pradesh's total population.
