121.src: APPSC Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Group-III Services Screening Test 2019 (Notification No.13/2018), Part A General Studies, held 21-04-2019 · Q46
121.x: Census 2011 put India's literacy rate at 74.04%.

122.s: Which state accounted for maximum number of human trafficking cases in 2016?
122.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
122.x: NCRB Crime in India 2016: West Bengal reported the most human-trafficking cases (3,579, about 44% of the national total), ahead of Rajasthan (1,422). Maharashtra and Delhi were far lower.

122.s:
Which of the following is / are included in the Directive Principles of State Policy?
A. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
B. Prohibition of consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of other drugs which are injurious to health
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
122.x: Only B is a Directive Principle: Article 47 asks the State to prohibit, except for medicinal purposes, intoxicating drinks and harmful drugs. A (prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour) is Article 23, a Fundamental Right (Right against Exploitation), not a DPSP.

122.s: The Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act (SITA), 1956 was renamed in 1986 as the:
o: Protection of Women from Exploitation Act
122.x: SITA (1956) became the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act in 1986.

122.s: The practice of Jogin in Telangana is more prevalent in the district of
122.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
122.x: Among the options the Jogini practice is most prevalent in the old Mahbubnagar district (about 2,000 Joginis in Mahbubnagar alone); Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam have it only marginally. (A printed key of Karimnagar is not supported.)

122.s: The Age group of a girl to be converted as Jogini is
122.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
122.x: Girls were usually dedicated as Joginis (Devadasis) at a young age, about 8–12 years; the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act 1988 bans it.

122.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh rehabilitates Jogin women through APSCCFC economic-support schemes.
Reason (R): The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in 2006.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
122.x: A is true. R is false: the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act dates from 1988/89, not 2006.

122.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The approach to suicide, beggary and drug abuse has shifted from punishment towards health and rehabilitation.
Reason (R): The Mental Healthcare Act 2017, SMILE and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan have taken the place of punitive tools like Sec. 309 IPC and begging laws.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
122.x: Both are true and R explains A: MHCA 2017, SMILE and NMBA embody the shift away from punishment (Sec. 309, begging laws) to health and rehabilitation.

122.s: 'Dharya Sparsa - Operation Flush-Out' against drugs and illegal liquor in Andhra Pradesh was launched by the police of:
122.x: The Chittoor Police launched the operation.

122.s: The chronic use of drugs and alcohol results in
122.x: Chronic alcohol and drug use scars the liver (cirrhosis) and damages the nervous system. Leukaemias and lymphomas are blood cancers not typical of drug/alcohol abuse; the other options are not its characteristic effects.

122.s: As per the statistics of the National Crime Records Bureau (ADSI 2015), the biggest reason for suicide of farmers in India is
122.src: APPSC Group-I Services Screening Test (Notification No. 36/2016) - General Studies & Mental Ability (single paper, Booklet Series A), held 07-05-2017 · Q11
122.x: NCRB's ADSI 2015 report listed bankruptcy or indebtedness as the leading cause of farmer suicides (about 38.7%).
o: illness, drug abuse and alcohol addiction

123.s: Which Constitutional Article gives the States the right to promote educational interests of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes of India?
123.src: Assistant BC, Social, Tribal Welfare Officer Screening Test
123.x: Article 46 (DPSP) directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, in particular SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.

123.s: Which of the following practices leads to social exclusion?
123.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
123.x: Separate (segregated) special schools keep blind children apart from mainstream schooling, so they lead to exclusion; inclusive education in ordinary schools is the alternative. Segregation is one of the practices of exclusion.

123.s:
Which of the following is mainly considered for relation to social exclusion?
A. Caste
B. Gender
C. Race
D. Tribes
Choose the correct answer.
123.x: Social exclusion is studied along caste, gender, race/ethnicity and tribe (and religion, disability, region), so all four (A, B, C, D) apply.

123.s: What is the main objective of providing reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes under the Indian Constitution?
o: To provide them free education abroad
To achieve social justice and equal opportunity
123.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer Paper-III (Indian Con
123.x: Reservations for SCs, STs and OBCs (Arts. 15(4), 16(4), 330, 332) aim at social justice and equality of opportunity for historically excluded groups; the other options are absurd.

123.s: Under which article of the Constitution are the states given right to promote the educational interests of the Scheduled castes and Scheduled tribes and other backward classes of India?
123.x: Article 46 (DPSP) asks the State to promote the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, especially SCs and STs.

123.s:
Social exclusion results in the following:
A. Adversely effecting human capital development
B. Bridging historical divisions
C. Widening inequalities
D. Driving social unrest and crime
Select the correct answer:
123.x: Social exclusion hurts human-capital development, widens inequalities and can drive unrest and crime (A, C, D). 'Bridging historical divisions' is the opposite – exclusion deepens them.

123.s: Which of the following is NOT a practice leading to social exclusion?
o: Denied access to land and water
123.x: Untouchability, segregation and denied access to land, water and jobs lead to exclusion; MGNREGA wage employment is a policy response to it.

123.s: The term 'social exclusion' was coined in France in 1974 by:
123.x: Rene Lenoir coined it; social exclusion is an involuntary and systematic process.

123.s: Which of the following statements about social exclusion is correct?
o: Denial of property to women is exclusion based on caste.
It is an involuntary and systematic process.
It is always a voluntary choice.
The term was coined by Amartya Sen.
123.x: The term is Rene Lenoir's; denial to women is gender-based exclusion.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In August 2026 the Union opposed a creamy layer for SCs and STs.
Reason (R): Income alone is enough to end caste-based exclusion.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
123.x: A is true (10 Aug 2026). R is false: the Union's ground was the opposite – income alone does not end caste-based exclusion.

123.s:
Match List-I (Basis of social exclusion) with List-II (Example):
List-I
a. Caste
b. Gender
c. Disability
d. Race / tribe
List-II
i. Adivasis in remote areas
ii. Untouchability against SCs
iii. Segregated special schools
iv. Denial of property, work and mobility
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Caste – untouchability; gender – denial of property, work, mobility; disability – lack of access, segregated special schools; race/tribe – Adivasis in remote areas, racial discrimination.

123.s: MNREGA came into force in?
123.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
123.x:
MGNREGA was replaced — now the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 came into force on 1 July 2026 (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.156)
NREGA came into force on 2 February 2006, launched at Bandlapalli in Anantapur district (AP), in 200 districts first. (Now replaced by the VB-G RAM G Act from 1 July 2026.)

123.s: Who among the following are eligible to benefit from the ‘Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act’?
o: Adult members of only the scheduled caste and scheduled tribe households
Adult members of Below Poverty Line (BPL) households
Adult members of households of all backward communities
123.x:
MGNREGA was replaced — now the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 (in force 1 July 2026) guarantees 125 days per rural household (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.156)
Adult members of any rural household who volunteer for unskilled manual work are eligible; the Act is not limited to SC/ST, BPL or backward-class households. (Now VB-G RAM G, 125 days, from 1 July 2026.)

123.s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : MGNREGA (until its replacement on 1 July 2026) provided employment to at least one member of the eligible household for a minimum period of 100 days in a year.
Reason (R) : Right to employment is enumerated in Part III of the Constitution.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
123.x:
Updated to the latest (Nov 2026): MGNREGA was replaced by the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 from 1 July 2026, which guarantees 125 days per rural household per year. Source: https://www.outlookmoney.com/news/vb-g-ram-g-act-replaces-mgnrega-implementation-to-take-effect-from-july-1
the 100-day guarantee was replaced — now 125 days under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, in force 1 July 2026 (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.156)
A is true: MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage work a year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer. R is false: the right to work is a Directive Principle (Art. 41), not a Fundamental Right in Part III. (Now 125 days under VB-G RAM G from 1 July 2026.)

123.s: Select the one which is not the responsibility of Gram Sabha under the ‘Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005’.
o: The recommend projects to the gram panchayat and prepare list of possible works.
To receive application for work and issue a rated receive.
To monitor the execution of works within the gram panchayat.
To conduct regular social audits of all projects taken up within the gram panchayat.
123.x: The Gram Sabha recommends works, monitors them and conducts social audits. Receiving applications for work and issuing dated receipts is the Gram Panchayat's job, so option 2 is not the Gram Sabha's responsibility.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NREGA got the name Mahatma Gandhi NREGA when it was passed in 2005.
2. NREGA was passed by Parliament in August 2005.
3. NREGA came into force on 2 February 2006, starting in Anantapur district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Mahatma Gandhi name was added only by renaming on 2 October 2009.

123.s: Under MGNREGA, at least what proportion of the beneficiaries must be women?
123.x: At least one-third of the workers must be women; 100 days of work per rural household is guaranteed.

123.s: Under MGNREGA, an unemployment allowance is payable if work is not provided within how many days of demand?
123.x: The allowance is due if work is not given within 15 days.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 replaced MGNREGA from 1 July 2026.
Reason (R): The VB-G RAM G Act guarantees 125 days of work per rural household per year.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
123.x: Both are true (passed 18 Dec 2025, in force 1 July 2026; 125 days, wage floor ₹300/day), but the 125-day guarantee is a feature of the new Act, not the reason it replaced MGNREGA.

123.s: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the rural employment law, is administered by the Ministry of:
123.x: It is run by the Ministry of Rural Development; Andhra Pradesh ranked first in the first 45 days.

123.s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the Centre-State funding ratio for most States is:
123.x: Funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States; the wage floor is Rs 300 a day.

123.s: In which year the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was launched?
123.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Service
123.x: SGSY began on 1 April 1999, merging IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and allied schemes into one SHG-based self-employment programme.

123.s: Which was the first state to start EGS (Employment Guarantee Scheme) in rural areas?
123.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
123.x: Maharashtra started the first Employment Guarantee Scheme in 1972 (Act 1977), the model for NREGA; AP, Rajasthan and Haryana came later.

123.s:
Arrange the following in a chronological order:
a. SGSY
b. NREP
c. JRY
d. IRDP
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
123.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
123.x: IRDP (1978-79 pilot, nationwide 2 Oct 1980) → NREP (1980) → JRY (1989, merged NREP and RLEGP) → SGSY (1999). So d, b, c, a.

123.s: At present, with which name is Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (1999) implemented? A) B)
123.x: SGSY was restructured in 2011 as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, branded 'Aajeevika' (renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016). MGNREGA is wage employment, not SGSY's successor.

123.s: The objective of integrated Rural Development Program is to
o: Provide free housing to all urban poor
Help families who live below the poverty line to enhance their income, state of living & empowerment
Provide 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to every rural household
Build all-weather roads to connect unconnected villages
123.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
123.x: IRDP (1978-79 / 2 October 1980) aimed to lift rural BPL families above the poverty line through self-employment assets financed by subsidy and bank credit.

123.s:
Match List-I (Programme) with List-II (Feature):
List-I
a. TRYSEM (1979)
b. DWCRA (1982-83)
c. JRY (1989)
d. PMEGP (2008)
List-II
i. Merged PMRY and REGP
ii. Sub-scheme of IRDP for rural women
iii. Merged NREP and RLEGP
iv. Training rural youth for self-employment
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: TRYSEM – training rural youth for self-employment (IRDP component); DWCRA – IRDP sub-scheme so benefits reach rural women; JRY – merged NREP and RLEGP; PMEGP – merged PMRY and REGP (credit-linked subsidy through KVIC).

123.s: The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY, 1999) merged IRDP, TRYSEM and:
123.x: SGSY merged IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and allied schemes.

123.s: The credit-linked subsidy under PMEGP is routed through:
123.x: KVIC is the nodal agency for PMEGP.

123.s: The difference between urban and rural average monthly per capita expenditure, in India in 2011-12, was around:
123.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
123.x: NSS 68th round (2011-12, MMRP): average MPCE was about Rs 1,430 rural and Rs 2,630 urban, a gap of about Rs 1,200 (urban about 84% higher).

123.s: The main cause for poverty of rural and tribal people is?
123.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
123.x: The expected key is illiteracy: lack of education keeps rural and tribal people out of better jobs and perpetuates the cycle of poverty. Unemployment is itself largely a result of low education and skills; 'economic status' just restates poverty.

123.s: What is being poor compared with others in the same society called?
123.x: Relative poverty means being poor in comparison with others in the same society; absolute poverty is spending below a fixed poverty line.

123.s: The concept of the 'culture of poverty' was propounded in 1959 by:
123.x: Oscar Lewis introduced the 'culture of poverty'; Nurkse gave the 'vicious circle of poverty'.

123.s: India's official poverty line is based on:
123.x: The poverty line is fixed in terms of monthly per capita consumption expenditure.

123.s: India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is prepared by:
123.x: The National MPI is NITI Aayog's; absolute poverty uses a fixed MPCE poverty line.

123.s: Which Indian organization is responsible for estimating the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?
123.x: The National MPI is built by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI, and NITI Aayog (successor of the Planning Commission) is the nodal agency for poverty estimation. The RBI and the Finance Ministry do not estimate it.

123.s: As per NITI MPI 2023, which State had the lowest multidimensional poverty?
123.x: Kerala recorded the lowest MPI poverty and Bihar (33.76%) the highest.

123.s:
Match List-I (Body / survey) with List-II (Role):
List-I
a. NITI Aayog
b. NSO's HCES
c. PLFS
d. National MPI
List-II
i. Built with UNDP and OPHI
ii. Consumption survey about every 5 years
iii. Nodal agency for poverty estimation
iv. Standard for unemployment data
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: NITI Aayog – nodal agency for poverty estimation (uses NSSO data); HCES – about every 5 years, its MPCE sets the line; PLFS – standard for unemployment data; National MPI – NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI.

123.s: In the Periodic Labour Force Survey, the Current Weekly Status records activity over a reference period of:
123.x: CWS uses the last seven days; usual status uses a year, and Current Daily Status each day of the week.

123.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the:
123.x: PLFS is conducted by the NSO under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Multidimensional Poverty Index:
1. It has three equally weighted dimensions and 12 indicators.
2. Nutrition is an indicator of the standard-of-living dimension.
3. Bank accounts is an indicator of the standard-of-living dimension.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
123.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: nutrition is a health indicator, not a standard-of-living one.

123.s: According to NITI Aayog's National MPI 2023 (NFHS-5 data), which State had the highest multidimensional poverty headcount?
123.x: Bihar recorded the highest headcount (33.76%); India's figure was 14.96%.

123.s: As per National sample Survey Organization the unemployment rate in 2017-18 was a 45 year high at Y) was
123.x: NSO's first PLFS (2017-18) put the unemployment rate at 6.1%, the highest since 1972-73 ('45-year high'), though NSO said the series is not strictly comparable. (Now 3.2% in 2023-24.)

123.s:
Match List-I (Type of unemployment) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I
a. Disguised
b. Structural
c. Cyclical
d. Frictional
List-II
i. Extra workers add near-zero output
ii. Temporary, while changing or searching for jobs
iii. Fall in labour demand in a slowdown
iv. Mismatch between skills and jobs
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Disguised – more workers than needed (agriculture); structural – skills–jobs mismatch; cyclical – slowdown cuts labour demand; frictional – temporary, while switching or searching.

123.s: Which of the following statements about unemployment in India is correct?
o: Disguised unemployment is mainly found in the urban labour market.
Educated unemployment is predominantly a rural phenomenon.
Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in agriculture.
Frictional unemployment is mainly found on family farms.
123.x: Seasonal unemployment is agricultural; disguised unemployment is found mainly on family farms, while educated and frictional unemployment are urban.

123.s: According to PLFS, India's unemployment rate (usual status) in 2023-24 was:
123.x: India's rate fell from 6.1 per cent in 2017-18 to 3.2 per cent in 2023-24; AP's was 4.1 per cent.

123.s: Which measure counts both the employed and the unemployed seeking work as a share of the population?
123.x: LFPR includes the employed and the job-seeking unemployed; WPR counts only the employed.

123.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what was poverty in 2023-24 as measured by the Tendulkar line?
123.x: Poverty measured by the Tendulkar line was stated to have fallen from 21.9 percent in 2011–12 to 2.3 percent in 2023–24.
123.tq: Distinguish the Tendulkar-line estimate from the MPI and World Bank estimates.
xs: Poverty on the **Tendulkar line** was **2.3 percent** in **2023-24** — option **(1)** (ES 2025-26).
**21.9%** was the earlier **2011-12** figure.
xa: Tendulkar 2004-05 estimate: **37.2%**.
Critics say the Tendulkar line is **too low**.
Income inequality is **rising** (World Inequality Database).

123.s:
Match List-I (Poverty estimation group) with List-II (Method):
List-I
a. Y.K. Alagh Task Force
b. Lakdawala Expert Group
c. Tendulkar Expert Group
d. Rangarajan Expert Group
List-II
i. Calories only: 2,400 rural, 2,100 urban
ii. Dropped the calorie anchor; Mixed Reference Period
iii. Food plus non-food needs such as housing and transport
iv. State-specific lines using CPI-AL and CPI-IW
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Alagh (1979) – calorie norms 2,400/2,100; Lakdawala (1993) – State-specific lines, CPI-AL rural and CPI-IW urban; Tendulkar (2009) – dropped calorie anchor, MRP, urban basket for both, health and education; Rangarajan (2014) – food + non-food.

123.s:
Match List-I (Committee) with List-II (Task):
List-I
a. Dandekar and Rath (1971)
b. Y.K. Alagh Task Force (1979)
c. S.R. Hashim Expert Group (2009)
d. N.C. Saxena Expert Group (2009)
List-II
i. Method of the rural BPL census
ii. Identifying urban BPL households
iii. Calorie-based spending norm
iv. First poverty-line study, 2,250 calories
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
123.x: Dandekar & Rath (1971) – first poverty-line study (2,250 calories); Alagh Task Force (1979) – spending needed to buy 2,400/2,100 calories; S.R. Hashim (2009) – urban BPL identification; N.C. Saxena (2009) – rural BPL census method.

123.s: According to the Tendulkar method, the poverty ratio in India in 2011-12 was:
123.x: Tendulkar poverty fell from 37.2% (2004-05) to 21.9% (2011-12).

123.s: Calorie norms of 2,400 (rural) and 2,100 (urban) were the basis of poverty estimates under the:
123.x: The calorie norms belong to the Alagh/Lakdawala method; Tendulkar moved away from calorie norms.

123.s: The Rangarajan Expert Group on poverty measurement (2012) was set up by the:
123.x: The Planning Commission set it up; NITI Aayog came only in 2015.

123.s: The Rangarajan poverty line for rural areas in 2011-12 was about how much per person per day?
123.x: Rangarajan put the line at Rs 32 a day rural and Rs 47 urban (Rs 972 and Rs 1,407 a month); Tendulkar's was about Rs 27 and Rs 33.

123.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In India, Scheduled Tribes have the highest incidence of poverty, followed by Scheduled Castes.
Reason (R): Discrimination and social exclusion, landlessness and remoteness keep these groups poor.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
123.x: Both are true and R explains A: the notes give discrimination, social exclusion, landlessness and remoteness as the cause of the ST > SC > others order.

123.s: India's social protection coverage, which was 22% in 2016, rose by 2025 to about:
123.x: Coverage rose to 64.3% in 2025, as per ILO data.

124.s: These rights enable men to have a reasonable and legal source of livelihood.
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Education & Data Processing Sec
124.x: Economic rights secure a person a reasonable and legal source of livelihood (work, wages, leisure). Liberty and religion are civil rights; education is a social-cultural right.

124.s: What is Magna Carta?
o: Charter of liberties signed by English King in AD 1215
124.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
124.x: Magna Carta (1215) is the charter of liberties signed by King John of England, the first document of the human-rights campaign. The other options are word-play distractors.

124.s: The Doctrine of Natural Rights as a part of the proposal for the spread of human rights was popularised by
124.x: John Locke popularised the doctrine of natural rights (life, liberty, property). Rousseau is known for the social contract and general will; Plato and Aristotle predate the natural-rights doctrine.

124.s: John Locke gave birth to the concept of human rights. He was a
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Animal Husbandry Assistant 2019
124.x: John Locke was an English (British) political thinker of the 17th century, author of the Two Treatises of Government. He was not American, German or French.

124.s: "Human rights serve as the protective Shield to the individuals whenever the state attempts to interfere with the civil liberties of individuals". This was stated by
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Village Sericulture Assistant 2019
124.x: The idea of rights as a protective shield (trumps) for the individual against State interference with civil liberties is Ronald Dworkin's; 'Ronald Darwin' is a garbled print of his name. Rousseau, Plato and Aristotle did not frame rights this way.

124.s: Name the French revolutionary who wrote ‘Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen’.
124.x: Olympe de Gouges wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen (1791) during the French Revolution. Mary Wollstonecraft wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman; Robespierre was a revolutionary leader.

124.s: The theory of ‘Natural Rights’ was propounded by
124.x: John Locke propounded the theory of natural rights to life, liberty and property. Hobbes, Bentham (utilitarianism) and Marx are linked to other theories.

124.s:
Which of the following is/are instance(s) of violation of human rights?
I. A person was detained by the security forces while going for casting vote in Parliamentary Election.
II. A civilian was killed by the Army while undertaking combing operation.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
124.x: Both are violations: detaining a person on the way to vote denies political participation, and killing a civilian in a combing operation violates the right to life.

124.s: The concept of Human Rights primarily emphasizes on
o: Dignity of Man as a Human Being
124.x: Human rights rest on the dignity of man as a human being; the UDHR Preamble begins with the inherent dignity and equal rights of all. Property, equality and religion are particular rights, not the core idea.

124.s: Take the case of dignity and equal rights for women. How do democrates help?
o: Women in democracies have equal degree of political representation in legislature.
Women in democracies have guaranteed rights and are always treated with respect.
Women in democracies are not subjected to sex discrimination in most aspects of social life.
In democracies, the principle of equality is accepted as legal norm, which makes it easier to guarantee their freedom and dignity.
124.x: In democracies equality is accepted as a legal norm, which makes it easier to guarantee women's freedom and dignity. The other options overstate: democracies do not ensure equal representation or that women are always respected.

124.s: 'Respect for human rights and responsibilities' is a
124.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Education & Data Processing Sec
124.x: Respect for human rights and responsibilities is a constitutional value, flowing from the Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties, rather than a merely civic, religious or economic value.

124.s: The person who described Human Rights as the new standards of civilisation.
124.x: Jack Donnelly described human rights as 'a new standard of civilization' (International Affairs, 1998); 'John Dowski' is a garbled print of his name. Plato, Aristotle and Rousseau did not use the phrase.

124.s: Who made the famous statement "Man is born free, but everywhere he is in chains."?
124.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
124.x: 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains' opens Rousseau's The Social Contract (1762); Locke, Mirabeau and Voltaire did not write it.

124.s: What Rights are Human Rights ?
o: Rights which are provided by Constitution of India
Rights provided to all human beings by nature
124.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Welfare & Development Secret
124.x: Human rights are the rights all human beings have by nature, simply as humans. Constitutional or fundamental rights are those a State grants; mere desires are not rights.

124.s: Right to vote is:
124.x: The right to vote is a political right (participation in government). In India it is a statutory right (Sec. 62, RP Act 1951), not a Fundamental Right.

124.s: Social rights will not include
124.x: Social rights protect groups such as women, children and Adivasis; 'care for political section' is not a social right (garbled option).

124.s: The Vienna Declaration (1993) affirmed that human rights are:
o: Only civil and political in nature
124.x: The Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action stressed the indivisibility of human rights.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In India the right to vote is not a Fundamental Right.
Reason (R): The right to vote in India is a statutory right under Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
124.x: Both are true and R explains A: the right to vote, a political right, is only a statutory right (Sec. 62, RP Act 1951), not part of Part III.

124.s:
Match List-I (Document / event) with List-II (Year):
List-I
a. Magna Carta
b. Glorious Revolution, England
c. US Declaration of Independence
d. French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
List-II
i. 1688
ii. 1215
iii. 1776
iv. 1789
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: Magna Carta – 1215 (King John); Glorious Revolution – 1688 (Bill of Rights 1689); US Declaration of Independence – 1776; French Declaration of the Rights of Man – 1789.

124.s:
Match List-I (Thinker) with List-II (Work / idea):
List-I
a. J.J. Rousseau
b. Olympe de Gouges
c. Mary Wollstonecraft
d. John Locke
List-II
i. 'Man is born free, but everywhere he is in chains'
ii. A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792)
iii. Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen (1791)
iv. Natural rights – life, liberty, property
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: Rousseau – the chains line (Social Contract, 1762); Olympe de Gouges – Declaration of the Rights of Woman (1791); Mary Wollstonecraft – A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792), not the 1791 Declaration; Locke – natural rights.

124.s: The Indian Civil Liberties Union, founded in 1936, was set up on the initiative of:
124.x: Nehru and others founded the ICLU in August 1936.

124.s: World Health Day is observed every year on:
124.x: World Health Day is 7 April; Human Rights Day is 10 December.

124.s: When is International Human Rights Day observed?
124.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
124.x: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, the day the UNGA adopted the UDHR in 1948. 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti/Non-Violence Day, 14 November Children's Day in India.

124.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights equates ___ with unemployment, sickness, disability and old age with the right to a standard of living adequate for the health and well-being of herself and of her family, including food, clothing, housing and medical care.
124.x: UDHR Art. 25(1) gives the right to security in the event of unemployment, sickness, disability, widowhood and old age, with an adequate standard of living. Divorce, adolescence and immigration are not listed there.

124.s: The theme of World Human Rights Day observed in December, 2016 was
o: Stand up for someone's rights today
124.x: The theme of Human Rights Day 2016 was 'Stand up for someone's rights today'. 'Our Rights, Our Freedoms, Always' was the 2015 theme.

124.s: The theme of World Human Rights Day observed in December, 2016 was
o: Stand up for someone's rights today
124.x: The theme of Human Rights Day 2016 was 'Stand up for someone's rights today'. 'Our Rights, Our Freedoms, Always' was the 2015 theme.

124.s: The theme of World Human Rights Day observed in December, 2016 was
o: Stand up for someone’s rights today
124.x: Human Rights Day 2016 had the theme 'Stand up for someone's rights today'. 'Our Rights, Our Freedoms, Always' was the 2015 theme; the others are not the 2016 theme.

124.s: When was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted by the United Nations?
124.x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948 in Paris. 24 October 1945 is the date the UN came into being.

124.s: 10th December is celebrated as –
124.x: 10 December is Human Rights Day, marking the UDHR's adoption in 1948 (UNGA resolution 423(V), 1950). World Health Day is 7 April, UN Day 24 October, Labour Day 1 May.

124.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by UN General Assembly, doesnot include which of the following?
o: Freedom of Adequate Standard of Living
124.x: The UDHR covers dignity, liberty and equality (Art. 1), the right to life (Art. 3) and an adequate standard of living (Art. 25), but not a right to universal basic income.

124.s: Which of the following is not considered to be one of the Human Rights listed by the United Nations?
124.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (None of the above); it is added as option 5.
All four printed rights are in the UDHR: freedom and equality (Art. 1), life and liberty (Art. 3), education (Art. 26) and privacy (Art. 12: no arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home or correspondence). So none is outside the UN list (official JPSC key: Right to Privacy).

124.s: How many Articles are there in ‘Universal Declaration of Human Rights’?
124.x: The UDHR has a Preamble and 30 Articles.

124.s: Which day is the ‘International Human Rights Day’?
124.x: Human Rights Day is 10 December, the day the UDHR was adopted in 1948. 24 October is UN Day.

124.s: When is the International Child Rights Day is celebrated?
124.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
124.x: Universal (International) Children's Day is 20 November, the date the UNGA adopted the Declaration (1959) and the Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989). 14 November is Children's Day in India.

124.s: Which human rights document helps to guide the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Agenda?
124.x: The UDHR covers civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights and guides the SDGs Agenda. The Paris Agreement (climate), Magna Carta and NAFTA (trade) are not its guide.

124.s: Universal Declaration of Human Rights is a
o: Declaration adopted by several Nations at an International Conference
124.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
124.x: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly as resolution 217 A on 10 December 1948; it is a declaration, not a treaty.

124.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights covers which rights?
o: Civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights
Only civil and political rights of individual citizens
Only economic, social and cultural rights of workers
124.x: The UDHR covers all five categories of rights, though it is not a treaty and is not legally binding as one.
xa: Binding covenants came later: **ICCPR** and **ICESCR** (adopted **16 Dec 1966**).
**International Bill of Human Rights** = **UDHR + ICCPR + ICESCR** + optional protocols.
Adopted by the **UNGA** on **10 December 1948**.

124.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948 at:
124.x: The UDHR was adopted at the Palais de Chaillot, Paris.

124.s: Which of the following statements about the UDHR is correct?
o: Its drafting committee was chaired by Rene Cassin.
It is not a legally binding treaty.
Human Rights Day was fixed in 1948 itself.
It has a Preamble and 40 articles.
124.x: The UDHR (Preamble and 30 articles) is not binding; Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the drafting body and Human Rights Day was fixed in 1950.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The UDHR is not legally binding on UN member States.
Reason (R): The UDHR is a declaration adopted by a UN General Assembly resolution, not a treaty.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
124.x: Both are true. R explains A: the UDHR is a declaration adopted by a General Assembly resolution, not a treaty.

124.s:
Match List-I (UDHR Article) with List-II (Right):
List-I
a. Article 3
b. Article 12
c. Article 23
d. Article 26
List-II
i. Work
ii. Life, liberty and security
iii. Education
iv. Privacy
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: Art. 3 – life, liberty, security; Art. 12 – privacy (also ICCPR Art. 17); Art. 23 – work; Art. 26 – education.

124.s: Universal Children's Day, observed on 20 November, marks the adoption of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in:
124.x: The UNCRC was adopted on 20 November 1989.

124.s: Human Rights Day is observed every year on:
124.x: Human Rights Day (10 December) marks the adoption of the UDHR in 1948.

124.s: Amnesty International is
o: an agency of the United Nations to help refugees of civil wars
a non-governmental voluntary organisation to help very poor people
an inter-governmental agency to cater to medical emergencies in war-ravaged regions
124.x: Amnesty International (London, 1961) is a global human rights movement, an NGO; it is not a UN refugee agency, a poverty-relief body or an inter-governmental medical agency.

124.s: Amnesty International is –
o: An agency of the United Nations to help refugees of civil wars
A non-governmental voluntary organization to help very poor people
An inter-governmental agency to cater to medical emergencies in war-ravaged regions
124.x: Amnesty International is a global movement campaigning against human-rights abuses, founded in 1961 by British lawyer Peter Benenson, headquartered in London. It is not a UN or inter-governmental agency.

124.s: Which one is not related to United Nations?
124.x: The General Assembly, ICJ and Trusteeship Council are principal UN organs; Amnesty International is an NGO with no UN status.

124.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Organisation)
A. Amnesty International
B. Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)
C. Danube Commission
D. European Space Agency
List-II (Associated Convention / Person / Place / Headquarters)
1. Viskuli
2. Paris
3. Peter Benenson
4. Belgrade Convention
Which of the following is correctly matched?
124.x: Amnesty International – Peter Benenson (A-3); CIS – Viskuli agreement, Belarus (B-1); Danube Commission – Belgrade Convention (C-4); European Space Agency – Paris HQ (D-2).

124.s: Amnesty International, founded in London in 1961, was founded by:
124.x: Peter Benenson founded Amnesty; it won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

124.s: Which of the following statements about human rights bodies is correct?
o: Human Rights Watch is based in New York.
The UN Human Rights Prize is awarded by the Human Rights Council.
Amnesty International was founded in Geneva.
Amnesty International won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987.
124.x: Amnesty was founded in London (1961) and won the Nobel in 1977; the UN prize is given by the General Assembly.

124.s: In July 2022, UN General Assembly adopted a historic resolution declaring access to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment, a universal _______.
124.x: On 28 July 2022 the UNGA recognised access to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment as a universal human right.

124.s: United Nations Human Rights Council(UNHRC) has 47 UN member states with specific number of seats allotted for each five regions of the globe. How many seats are allotted for Asia-Pacific States.
124.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
124.x: Of the UN Human Rights Council's 47 seats, the Asia-Pacific group holds 13 (as does Africa); Latin America 8, Western Europe and Others 7, Eastern Europe 6.

124.s: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Declaration on the Right to Development?
124.x: The right to development was recognised by a UNGA Declaration in 1986.

124.s:
Match the following regional groups with their seats in the UN Human Rights Council:
List-I
A. Africa
B. Latin America and Caribbean
C. Western Europe and Others
D. Eastern Europe
List-II
1. 6
2. 7
3. 8
4. 13
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
124.x: Of the 47 seats, Africa has 13, Latin America and Caribbean 8, Western Europe and Others 7 and Eastern Europe 6.

124.s: Which one of the following statements about the UN Human Rights Council is correct?
o: Its members are elected by the UN Security Council
Its members are elected by the UN General Assembly for three-year terms
A member can serve any number of consecutive terms
It is based in New York
124.x: The 47-member Council (Geneva, 2006) is elected by the UNGA; members may serve at most two consecutive terms and can be suspended by a two-thirds UNGA vote.

124.s: The Universal Periodic Review of the human rights record of every UN member is conducted by the:
124.x: The UPR, begun in 2008, is run by the Human Rights Council.

124.s: The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) was set up in 1993 following the:
o: Vienna World Conference on Human Rights
124.x: The OHCHR was set up after the 1993 Vienna Conference.

124.s: The National Human Rights Commission of India is a:
o: Executive body under a Cabinet resolution
Statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
124.x: The NHRC was set up under the PHRA, 1993, in line with the Paris Principles.

124.s: The Paris Principles relating to national human rights institutions were adopted by the UN General Assembly in:
124.x: They were drafted in Paris in 1991 and adopted by the UNGA in 1993.

124.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment is a third-generation (collective) human right.
Reason (R): The UN General Assembly recognised the Right to Water and Sanitation on 28 July 2010.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
124.x: Both are true – a healthy environment is a collective, third-generation right (UNGA recognition 28 July 2022), and water and sanitation was recognised on 28 July 2010 – but R does not explain A.

124.s: Which one of the following is considered to be the second generation of Human Rights ?
124.x:
Most books and keys: Right to Education. Strictly: the Right to Work (ICESCR Art. 6) is equally a second-generation right, so that option is also correct; the stem is loose (general knowledge, not checked).
In Vasak's scheme the second generation (equality) covers economic, social and cultural rights, so the Right to Education is the expected answer. Liberty and Equality before law are first-generation rights.

124.s: The classification of human rights into three generations was proposed in 1977 by:
124.x: Karel Vasak linked the three generations with liberty, equality and fraternity.

124.s: Third-generation human rights are linked with the ideal of:
124.x: First generation – liberty (civil-political); second – equality (social-economic); third – fraternity (solidarity).

124.s: Child Rights are protected in Article_______of ICCPR.
124.x: Article 24 of the ICCPR protects the rights of the child (protection, name, nationality). Art. 21 is peaceful assembly and Art. 23 family; Art. 24 of the Indian Constitution also concerns children (child labour).

124.s: In which year was the Optional Protocol to the ICESCR adopted?
124.x: The ICESCR Optional Protocol was adopted in 2008; 1976 is when the two Covenants entered into force.

124.s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 is associated with which treaty and what change in the number of recognised disabilities?
124.x: The CRPD concerns persons with disabilities and gave rise to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, which raised recognised disabilities from 7 to 21.
124.tq: Link the treaty, implementing legislation and numerical change as one factual chain.
xs: The **RPwD Act, 2016** flows from the **CRPD** and raised recognised disabilities **from 7 to 21** — option **(4)**.
**CPED** is on **enforced disappearance** and **CEDAW** on **discrimination against women**; option (1) reverses the numbers.
xa: CRPD adopted **2006**; India **ratified 2007**.
**CPED** (**2006**) — India **signed 2007, not ratified**.
**CMW** (**1990**, migrant workers) — India **not signed**.

124.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the International Bill of Human Rights?
124.x: The International Bill comprises the UDHR, the ICCPR, the ICESCR and their optional protocols.

124.s: India acceded to the ICCPR and the ICESCR in:
124.x: India acceded to both Covenants in 1979 but has not signed the ICCPR First Optional Protocol.

124.s:
Match List-I (ICCPR Article) with List-II (Right):
List-I
a. Article 6
b. Article 7
c. Article 14
d. Article 19
List-II
i. Fair trial
ii. Life
iii. Freedom from torture
iv. Expression
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: ICCPR: Art. 6 – life; Art. 7 – no torture; Art. 14 – fair trial; Art. 19 – expression (privacy is Art. 17, child rights Art. 24).

124.s:
Match List-I (Convention) with List-II (Subject):
List-I
a. CERD
b. CMW
c. CPED
d. CRPD
List-II
i. Persons with disabilities
ii. Enforced disappearance
iii. Migrant workers
iv. Racial discrimination
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
124.x: CERD (1965) – racial discrimination, ratified by India 1968; CMW (1990) – migrant workers, not signed; CPED (2006) – enforced disappearance, signed 2007; CRPD (2006) – disabilities, ratified 2007.

124.s: Which of the following UN human rights treaties has India NOT ratified?
o: Convention on the Rights of the Child
124.x: India signed the Convention against Torture in 1997 but has not ratified it.

124.s: India acceded to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in:
124.x: India acceded on 11 December 1992; it ratified CEDAW in 1993.

125.s: Article prohibits untouchability in any form in the Constitution
125.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Art. 14 is equality before law, Art. 16 equality in public employment, Art. 19 the six freedoms.

125.s: The Article in which 'Prohibition of Untouchability' is incorporated
125.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Art. 14 is equality before law, Art. 16 equality in public employment, Art. 19 the six freedoms.

125.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution Guarantees the Right to Equality?
125.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
125.x: Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws. Art. 19 gives the six freedoms, Art. 21 life and liberty, Art. 25 freedom of religion.

125.s: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution professes that State shall not deny any person 'Equality before the law'?
125.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
125.x: Article 14: the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. Arts. 11-13 deal with citizenship law, the definition of State and laws inconsistent with FRs.

125.s: ___ prohibits traffic in human beings and 'begar' and other similar forms of forced labour.
125.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
125.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour. Art. 27 is about taxes for religion, Art. 33 about armed forces, Art. 37 about DPSP enforceability.

125.s: Which Article of Indian Constitution says that 'untouchability' is abolished?
125.x: Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability. Art. 18 abolishes titles, Art. 14 is equality before law, Art. 3 is about new States.

125.s: Article 23 of the Indian Constitution prohibits
o: Traffic in human beings and forced labour
125.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar). Untouchability is Art. 17; discrimination is barred by Art. 15.

125.s:
Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India?
1. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
2. Abolition of untouchability
3. Protection of the interests of minorities
4. Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
125.x: The Right against Exploitation is Arts. 23 (traffic and forced labour) and 24 (no child below 14 in factories, mines). Untouchability (Art. 17) is under the Right to Equality and minorities are under Arts. 29-30, so 1 and 4 only.

125.s: Which one of the following is a fundamental right under the constitution of India and a human right as well
125.x: Art. 21A makes education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right as well as a human right (UDHR Art. 26). Information is statutory, and housing and a right to die are not Fundamental Rights.

The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act is known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xs: The **106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023** is the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** — option **(4)**.
It extends **not less than one-third** reservation to the **Lok Sabha**, **State Assemblies** and the **Delhi** Assembly.
xa: It passed as the **128th Amendment Bill** (**21 Sept 2023**).
Local-body reservation came earlier via the **73rd and 74th Amendments, 1992**.
The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** to fast-track it was **defeated** (**17 Apr 2026**).

131.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to women's reservation in chronological order:
A. Constitution (106th Amendment) Act enacted
B. 108th Amendment Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha
C. 81st Amendment Bill introduced
D. 108th Amendment Bill lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha
131.x: The 81st Amendment Bill was introduced in 1996, the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.
131.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest Bill and the final enacted amendment.
xs: Correct order is **C, B, D, A** — option **(1)**.
C: **81st Amendment Bill** introduced in **1996** (Deve Gowda govt).
B: **108th Amendment Bill** passed by the **Rajya Sabha** on **9 March 2010**.
D: the 108th Bill **lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha** in **2014**; A: **106th Amendment** enacted in **2023**.
xa: The 81st Bill **lapsed with the 11th Lok Sabha**; it was reintroduced in **1998, 1999, 2002-03** (Vajpayee govts) and lapsed again.
The 108th Bill was **introduced in the Rajya Sabha** in **2008**.
The 2023 measure was the **128th Amendment Bill**, passed on **21 Sept 2023**.

131.s: For which Assemblies was the women's reservation under the 106th Amendment in force from 17 April 2026?
o: Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep
National Capital Territory of Delhi only
131.x: The reservation was stated to be in force for the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies from 17 April 2026.
131.tq: Match the effective date with the exact pair of Assemblies named.
xs: The quota was in force for the **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies from **17 April 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
For the Delhi Assembly the quota comes through **Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**, but the notes list only **J&K and Puducherry** as in force.
xa: Nationally, commencement waits for the **2027 Census** and delimitation (not before **2034**).
The same day, **17 April 2026**, the **131st Amendment Bill** was defeated in the Lok Sabha.
The quota includes **one-third of SC/ST reserved seats**.

131.s: On which date did the President give assent to the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
131.x: Parliament passed the Bill on 21 September 2023 and the President gave assent on 28 September 2023.

131.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. It reserves one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly for women, including one-third of SC/ST seats.
2. It also reserves one-third of seats for women in the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils.
3. It provides an OBC sub-quota within the women's reservation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
131.x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils are not covered. 3 is wrong: there is no OBC sub-quota.

a. 330A
b. 332A
c. 239AA(2)(ba)

131.x: 330A – Lok Sabha; 332A – State Assemblies; 239AA(2)(ba) – Delhi Legislative Assembly; 334A – starts after the first Census after the Act and delimitation, lasts 15 years (extendable).

131.s: Under Article 334A, seats reserved for women in the Lok Sabha will rotate:
o: Every five years by Presidential order
Every ten years by the Election Commission
131.x: Rotation is after each delimitation; the 15-year period can be extended only by Parliament by law.

131.x: It was introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill; the 108th Bill had passed the Rajya Sabha in 2010 and lapsed in 2014.

131.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026.
Reason (R): The Bill sought to raise the strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

131.x: The 106th Amendment (2023) inserted Articles 330A and 332A, effective after Census-based delimitation.

131.s: Which of the following measures came first in empowering women politically in India?
o: Setting up the National Commission for Women
Reserving seats for women in local bodies
Introducing the Women's Reservation Bill for legislatures
131.x: Reserving seats for women in local bodies came first (73rd/74th Amendments) and is the APPSC 2007 key. The NCW, SHGs and a Reservation Bill for legislatures came after, so they are not the answer.
131.tq: Local-body reservation first; legislature quota (106th) came much later.
xs: **Reserving seats for women in local bodies** came first — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2007** key).
The **NCW**, women's **SHGs** and the **Reservation Bill** for legislatures came after it.
Local-body reservation came through **Art. 243D(3)** (panchayats) and **Art. 243T(3)** (municipalities).
xa: The **73rd Amendment** came into force on **24 April 1993**.
**NCW** was set up in **1992** under the **NCW Act 1990**.
**Bihar** was the first State to give women **50%** in local bodies (**2006**).

Their ability to influence the direction of social change

To authorize a person for extra investigation other than the police
To remove a person from the area who is suspected to commit an offence
Take measurement and photograph of a person who is likely to commit an offence

Enhanced punishment for public servants in specified circumstances
Cancellation of arms licences in atrocity-prone areas
Automatic dissolution of every local authority located in an atrocity-prone area

The Act **cancels arms licences** of potential offenders in **atrocity-prone areas** and gives **licences to SC/ST persons**.
It gives **enhanced minimum punishment** for public servants.
xa: States identify **atrocity-prone areas**.
**Sec. 4** punishes **wilful neglect of duty**.

144.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

144.s: According to which article, the right of minorities to establish and administer minorities educational institutions?
144.x: Article 30(1): all minorities, religious or linguistic, may establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. Article 29 is about conserving language, script and culture.

144.s:
Match List I (Article of Indian Constitution) with List II (Provisions) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
List I (Article of Indian Constitution)
A. Article 16(2)
B. Article 29(2)
C. Article 30(1)
D. Article 31(1)
List II (Provisions)
1. No person shall be deprived of his property save by the authority of law
2. No person can be discriminated against in the matter of public appointment on the ground of race, religion or caste
3. All minorities whether based on religion or language shall have the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice
4. No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State, or receiving State aid, on grounds of religion, race, caste, language or any of them
Codes:
144.x: 16(2) is no discrimination in public employment (2), 29(2) no denial of admission (4), 30(1) minorities' institutions (3) and old 31(1) no deprivation of property save by law (1), giving A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1.

144.s: Which Article of the Constitution protects the 'Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice'?
144.x: Article 30 protects the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions; Art. 29 protects the interests of minorities, Art. 26 religious affairs and Art. 19 freedoms.

144.s: A State seeks to deny aid to an educational institution solely because it is managed by a linguistic minority. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
144.x: Article 30(2) provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.
144.tq: Apply the factual situation to the specific clause dealing with State aid to minority-managed institutions.
xs: **Article 30(2)** — the State shall not discriminate against **minority-managed** institutions in **granting aid** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 29(1)** is about conserving language/culture, **29(2)** about admission, and **350A** about mother-tongue primary instruction.
xa: **Art. 30(1)** covers **all minorities, religious or linguistic** — the "Charter of Education Rights".
**Art. 30(1A)** was added by the **44th Amendment**.

144.s: Where is the headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities?
144.x: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities has its headquarters in New Delhi: set up there in 1957, moved to Allahabad (Prayagraj) for a time, and back in New Delhi since 2015. (Earlier app key: Prayagraj.)

144.s:
Match List I (Article) with List II (Provision):
List I (Article)
a. Article 29(1)
b. Article 29(2)
c. Article 30(1A)
d. Article 30(2)

1. Compensation on compulsory acquisition of a minority institution's property must not abridge the right
2. No discrimination in grant of aid because an institution is under minority management
3. Right of a section of citizens to conserve its distinct language, script or culture
4. No denial of admission to State-maintained or State-aided institutions on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
144.x: Art. 29(1) = conserve language, script or culture; 29(2) = no denial of admission; 30(1A) (44th Amendment, 1978) = compensation on acquisition of minority institution property; 30(2) = no discrimination in aid.

3. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities

o: Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956.
The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by each Governor.
Linguistic minorities are identified on an all-India basis.
The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

144.s:

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

Minority Rights aim at ensuring equality

144.x: Jains were notified as a minority on 27 January 2014, after the five of 1993, so they are the sixth.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the minorities in India:
1. The Government of India has notified five communities, namely, Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Buddhists and Zoroastrians as minorities.
2. The National Commission for Minorities was given statutory status in 1993.
3. The smallest religious minority in India are the Zoroastrians.
4. The Constitution of India recognizes and protects religious and linguistic minorities.
Which of these statements are correct ?
144.x:
Earlier app key: (c) 2, 3 and 4. Strictly statement 1 was true in 2001 and statement 3 is doubtful (Parsis are the smallest notified minority only); official UPSC key not seen.
In 2001 statement 1 was true (five communities were notified in 1993; Jains came only in 2014). The NCM became statutory under the 1992 Act, in force from May 1993, and the Constitution protects religious and linguistic minorities. Statement 3 fails strictly, because Parsis are the smallest notified minority but not the smallest religious community (Jews are fewer). (Earlier app key: 2, 3 and 4.)

144.s: "Minority" for the purpose of the National Commission for Minorities means Community notified as such by
144.x: Section 2(c) of the NCM Act 1992 defines a minority as a community notified as such by the Central Government.

144.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised because it gives the Centre:
o: exclusive power to appoint State minority commissions
power to amend the Constitution without Parliament
144.x: Section 2(c) has been criticised as giving the Centre ‘unbridled power’ to notify minorities, raising concerns in the context of T.M.A. Pai.
144.tq: Match the statutory provision with the specific constitutional criticism rather than a broader unrelated power.
xs: Critics say **Section 2(c)** gives the Centre **"unbridled power"** to **notify minorities** — option **(1)**.
It sits uneasily with **T.M.A. Pai (2002)**, which made the **State** the unit for minority status.
xa: The NCM Act does not define minority; a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
States may notify their own minorities — **Jains** in **11 States** before 2014.

144.s: Which is the largest notified minority community in India as per Census 2011?
144.x: Muslims form 14.2% of the population (Census 2011), the largest minority; Christians are 2.3% and Sikhs 1.7%.

144.x: T.M.A. Pai held that linguistic and religious minorities are to be determined State-wise.

144.s:

III. It can make recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards for the protection of minorities by Central or State Governments. (B) I and II only

144.x: The Chairperson and Members of the NCM are nominated by the Central (Union) Government, not appointed by the President.

Updated to the latest (Nov 2026): No newer official count was found; the last official figure (Lok Sabha answer, Dec 2017) is 18 States/UTs, so the stem is pinned to that year. Source: https://www.business-standard.com/article/government-press-release/state-minority-commissions-116120700973_1.html

144.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Conducting elections to minority educational institutions
Looking into specific complaints relating to deprivation of minority safeguards
Monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards for minorities

xs: **Conducting elections to minority educational institutions** is NOT an NCM function — option **(1)**.
NCM functions: evaluate minorities' **development**, **monitor constitutional and legal safeguards**, look into **specific complaints**, recommend measures, commission studies.

To remove the members of the commission parliament's Approval is required
144.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains

o: If Application to establish a minority educational Institution is rejected, the competent Authority shall communicate the same to the applicant

With reference to consumers rights/privileges under the provisions of law in India, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. Consumers are empowered to take samples for food testing.
2. When a consumer files a complaint in any Consumer Forum, no fee is required to be paid.
3. In the case of death of a consumer, his/her legal heir can file a complaint in the Consumer Forum on his/her behalf.
Select the correct answer using the code given below
146.x: 1 and 3 are right: consumers may have food samples tested, and a deceased consumer's legal heir may complain. A fee is payable above the free slab (nil only up to Rs 5 lakh now).

146.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six consumer rights recognised under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
146.x: The six rights include safety, information, choice, hearing, redressal and consumer awareness. A right to private ownership is not included in this list.
146.tq: Find the odd legal entitlement among the recognised consumer rights.
xs: The **right to private ownership** is NOT one of the six consumer rights — option **(3)**.
The six: **safety**, be **informed**, **choose**, be **heard**, **seek redressal**, **consumer awareness**.
xa: Consumers may get **food samples tested** (UPSC 2012 key).
A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.

146.s: Which one of the following persons would generally be treated as a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
o: A person purchasing services for commercial exploitation
A person purchasing goods solely for a large-scale business activity
A person purchasing goods for resale
A person making an online purchase for personal use
146.x: The definition includes online and electronic purchases for personal use. A person buying for resale or commercial use is generally excluded.
146.tq: Apply the personal-use and commercial-purpose distinction to a factual situation.
xs: A person making an **online purchase** for **personal use** is a consumer — option **(4)**.
The definition **includes online and electronic purchases**; a buyer for **resale/commercial use** is not a consumer.
xa: **"Advertisement"** includes electronic media, internet and websites.
A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.

146.s: What did the Supreme Court hold in Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha (1995)?
o: All medical services, including those rendered by private doctors for a fee, are outside the scope of consumer law.
Medical services paid for, including services in hospitals charging some patients, constitute “service” under the Consumer Protection Act.
Medical negligence can never be considered by consumer fora and must be taken only to civil courts or medical councils.
Only services provided free of charge in government hospitals and dispensaries are covered by consumer protection law.
146.x: The 1995 decision held that paid medical services, including services in hospitals that charge some patients, fall within the definition of service under consumer law. Wholly free services are excluded.
146.tq: Use the paid-versus-wholly-free distinction to identify the holding.
xs: **IMA v. V.P. Shantha (1995):** **paid medical services**, including those in hospitals charging some patients, are a **"service"** under the Consumer Protection Act — option **(2)**.
So **medical negligence** can go to consumer fora; only **wholly free** services are excluded.
xa: A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.
CPA 2019 brought **product liability** of service providers.

146.s: Which of the following statements about the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is correct?

151.s: Hambantota port in Sri Lanka is often cited as part of the encirclement of India by:
151.x: Hambantota, leased to a Chinese firm, is seen as part of China's 'string of pearls'.

151.s: Nepal's first elected President is

151.x: Ram Baran Yadav was elected the first President of Nepal in July 2008.

151.s: Who is the first Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal?
151.x: Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' became the first PM of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal in August 2008; Ram Baran Yadav was the first President.

151.s: The first Prime Minister of the Republic of Nepal was :
151.x: Prachanda (UCPN-Maoist) became the first PM of republican Nepal in August 2008.

151.s: According to 2022 Report of U.S. Department of State on International Religious Freedom, which of these religions has the highest population in Nepal (as per Census 2011)?
151.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
151.x: Nepal is a Hindu-majority country: Hinduism had about 81% of the population in the 2011 Census (the figure the US State Department report cites), far ahead of Buddhism (about 9%), Islam and Christianity.

151.s: Which treaty is associated with an open border and security cooperation, while Nepal seeks its revision?
o: India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950
151.x: The 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship provides for an open border and security cooperation; Nepal has sought its revision.
151.tq: Match the treaty's distinctive features with its correct bilateral relationship.
xs: The **India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950** provides an **open border** and **security cooperation**; **Nepal wants it revised** — option **(3)**.
The **Bhutan treaty** is **1949**; the **Land Boundary Agreement** (**1974**) exchanged enclaves; the **Ganga Water Treaty** (**1996**) is on water.
xa: In **2026**, Nepal's **youth-led leadership** is pushing to revise the **1950 Treaty**.
Other Nepal agreements: **Kosi (1954)**, **Gandak (1959)**, **Mahakali (1996)**.

151.s: What is the estimated hydropower potential of Nepal?
151.x: Nepal's hydropower potential is put at 83,000 MW; the first trilateral power deal had Nepal supplying Bangladesh through the Indian grid.
xa: Bhutan projects: **Mangdechhu** (**2019**), **Punatsangchhu I and II**.
Nepal projects: **Pancheshwar**, **Arun III**.

151.s: Under the first trilateral power deal in the region, through which route does Nepal supply electricity to Bangladesh?
151.x: Nepal supplies power to Bangladesh through the Indian grid, the first trilateral power trade.

151.s: Nepal's monarchy was abolished by its first Constituent Assembly in:
151.x: The monarchy was abolished on 28 May 2008; the new Constitution was adopted on 20 September 2015.

151.s: Which of the following statements about Nepal is correct?
o: Prachanda belonged to the Nepali Congress
Its new Constitution was adopted on 20 September 2015
151.x: The monarchy was abolished in 2008; Prachanda led the CPN (Maoist).

152.s: Which one of the following is not one of the objectives of Act East Policy?
o: To promote economic cooperation cultural ties and develop strategic relationship with countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
To promote peace and amity with the neighbouring countries of Asia.
To place emphasis on India ASEAN cooperation in India’s domestic agenda.
To provide enhanced connectivity to the North East of India.
152.x: MEA lists Act East's objectives as economic cooperation, cultural ties and strategic relationship with the Asia-Pacific, enhanced connectivity to the North-East, and India-ASEAN cooperation in the domestic agenda; 'peace and amity with neighbouring countries of Asia' is not one of them (that is closer to Neighbourhood First).

152.s: IMBEX is a joint exercise conducted regularly between Armies of India and
152.x: IMBEX (India-Myanmar Bilateral Exercise) is the regular army exercise between India and Myanmar.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about the India’s Look East Policy.
I. It was articulated during the reign of HD Deve Gowda as India’s Prime Minister.
II. It is directed towards South Asian Region.
III. It is about controlling terrorism.
IV. It seeks to develop a bond among various countries on the basis of economic cooperation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
152.x:
The printed stem says 'South Asian Region'; Look East was directed at South-East Asia, so strictly only IV is correct. The key 'II and IV' reads statement II as South-East Asia, as in the original NDA 2010 paper.
Statement I is wrong – Look East was articulated under P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991-92), not Deve Gowda; III is wrong – it was an economic, not a counter-terrorism, policy; IV is right. II is right only as the original question reads it – 'directed towards the South-East Asian region'; the stem's 'South Asian' is a misprint, since Look East never targeted South Asia.

152.s:
Which of the following is/are correct about East Asia Summit?
a. 13th East Asia Summit was held in Singapore
b. It is an ASEAN-Centered Forum
c. It can only be chaired by an ASEAN member
d. East Asia Summit comprises of the ten member states of the ASEAN
152.src: APPSC AEE Civil & Mechanical Engineering General Studies & M
152.x: a, b and c are correct: the 13th EAS was held in Singapore (Nov 2018), the EAS is ASEAN-centred and only an ASEAN member chairs it. d is wrong – the EAS has 18 members (10 ASEAN + 8 partners incl. India, China, USA, Russia).

152.s:
Which of the following is/are correct about East Asia Summit?
a. 13th East Asia Summit held in Singapore.
b. It is an ASEAN-Centered Forum.
c. It can only be chaired by an ASEAN Member.
d. East Asia Summit comprises the ten member states of the ASEAN.
152.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
152.x: a, b and c are correct: 13th EAS in Singapore (2018), ASEAN-centred, chaired only by an ASEAN member. d is wrong – the EAS has 18 members, not just the ten ASEAN states; so 'all of the above' is wrong.

152.s: The second edition of India Myanmar Naval Exercise IMNEX-2019 was organised at:
152.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
152.x: IMNEX-2019, the second India-Myanmar Naval Exercise, was held at Visakhapatnam (19-22 October 2019), like the first edition in 2018.

152.s:
Match List-I (Policy) with List-II (Associated with):
List-I
a. Look East
b. Act East
c. Neighbourhood First
d. Link West
List-II

ii. P.V. Narasimha Rao, 1991–92
iii. East Asia Summit in Myanmar, 2014
iv. Gulf, Iran and Israel

152.x: Look East – Narasimha Rao, 1991–92 (economic, ASEAN); Act East – launched at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar, 2014 (not a SAARC Summit); Neighbourhood First – May 2014 swearing-in with SAARC leaders; Link West/Think West – West Asia: Gulf, Iran, Israel.

152.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the '4 Cs' of India's Act East Policy?
152.x: The 4 Cs are Commerce, Culture, Connectivity and Capacity building; the North-East is the gateway to ASEAN.

152.s: The Akhaura-Agartala rail link connects India with:
152.x: Akhaura-Agartala is a link with Bangladesh; the Kaladan project and Trilateral Highway involve Myanmar.

152.s: Dustlik-2019 - a first ever joint military exercise was held between India and ___:
152.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
152.x: DUSTLIK is the India-Uzbekistan joint military exercise; its first edition was held in November 2019 at Tashkent.

152.s: What is the importance of developing Chabahar Port by India?
o: India's trade with African countries will enormously increase.
India's relations with oil-producing Arab countries will be strengthened.
India will not depend on Pakistan for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
Pakistan will facilitate and protect the installation of a gas pipeline between Iraq and India.
152.x: Chabahar gives India an alternative route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan, which denies India land transit.

152.s: Through which port of Iran, India sent its consignment of wheat in October, 2017 to Afghanistan by passing the Pakistan route?
152.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
152.x: India's first wheat shipment to Afghanistan (October 2017) went through Iran's Chabahar port, bypassing Pakistan.

152.s: What bilateral trade target was set when India-Uzbekistan ties were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2026?
152.x: The August 2026 upgrade set a $5 billion trade target by 2030, along with a uranium-supply framework.
xa: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (**Samarkand, 2019**).
Other upgrades: **Vietnam** CSP **2016**; **Malaysia** CSP **2024**; **Philippines** strategic partner **Aug 2025**.

152.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the I2U2 grouping?
152.x: I2U2 is India, Israel, the US and the UAE; its first summit was virtual in 2022.
